Fact.Name: Has qualified business income
Fact.Description: Whether the taxpayer has net income from a qualified trade or business (not W-2 wages). Gate for the QBI deduction entry path.

Fact.Name: Who Can Take the Deduction, first limb — the filer has QBI from a qualified trade or business
Fact.Description:
THE FIRST LIMB of Form 8995's disjunctive admission test, and the return's answer to "do you have QBI". An explicit answer to /hasQbiIncome wins (including an explicit FALSE, which suppresses both auto-enable arms below). When /hasQbiIncome is UNANSWERED, this auto-enables for a filer with a positive Schedule C net profit (scheduleC:/hasScheduleCNetProfit) OR for a filer who has entered a qualified trade, business or aggregation into /qualifiedBusinesses and answered its qualified business income: §199A QBI is not a preparer election, so an eligible filer who never answered the QBI question still gets the deduction. Resolves Complete false when the question is unanswered, there is no Schedule C net profit, and no entered business carries an answered amount.
THE COLLECTION ARM IS NEW, and it is this own principle one intake later. Everything else in this body is /claimsQbiDeduction's, unchanged, moved here on the same day by the outer-gate rebody. That rebody discharged "QBI is not a preparer election" for the Schedule C route only, because at the time the manual QBI amount was a single return-level scalar. The collection migration replaced that scalar with /qualifiedBusinesses/*/writableQualifiedBusinessIncome; the collection arm below closes that gap - a filer who entered one or more businesses, held no Schedule C and never answered /hasQbiIncome would otherwise get FALSE here, $0 out of taxCalculations /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction's catch-all, and Form 1040 line 13a blank against a Form 8995 line 1 table they had filled in. Taxpayer-ADVERSE. Every committed case that populates the collection also answers /hasQbiIncome, so the arm moves nothing on the committed corpus.
EXISTENCE OF AN ANSWERED AMOUNT, NOT POSITIVITY OF THE TOTAL, and the printed form is what decides it rather than preference. Two rules were available: "any item answered" and "the netted total is above $0". Form 8995 line 1 column (c) is headed "Qualified business income or (loss)" and line 2 is "Total qualified business income or (loss)", so a LOSS column belongs on the very table this gate is about — a filer whose only business ran at a loss is properly on Form 8995 and is not outside its admission test. The Note above line 1 asks whether the filer HAS "qualified business income from a qualified trade or business"; an answered line 1(c) entry is exactly that, whatever its sign. The positivity rule would instead close the gate on a pure-loss return, which the printed table plainly admits.
AND THE TWO RULES COST NOTHING TO CHOOSE BETWEEN TODAY, which is what makes taking the plainer reading of the printed table the right call rather than a preference: on a pure-loss return both give a $0 deduction, because line 4's floor lives at the consumer's GreaterOf. WHAT WAS FORWARD-LOOKING HERE IS NOW SETTLED, and the answer is the one this paragraph hoped for. The section 199A(c)(2) carry-OUT (Form 8995 line 16) is at /qualifiedBusinessNetLossCarryforwardToNextYear, and it does NOT read this gate: it computes off the netted total on both of its arms, and /qbiSimplifiedAmount reports -20,000 on that case whichever rule this gate had taken. So the choice made here still costs nothing, and the loss on a pure-loss return now leaves the return by line 16 rather than being forgiven by either reading.
ANSWEREDNESS IS TESTED ON THE RAW WRITABLE, deliberately, because the complete-safe alias /qualifiedBusinesses/*/qualifiedBusinessIncome is ALWAYS Complete and therefore cannot tell an answered $0 from an unanswered field. An answered $0 opens the gate — a filer who enters a business and answers its QBI as $0 has made a deliberate determination, which is the same reading /qbiSimplifiedAmount's Description already gives that shape.
WHAT THE NEW ARM DOES NOT TOUCH, checked rather than assumed. (b) The FORM-SELECTION gate is untouched: /qbiUsesForm8995A is All(/claims8995A, Any(/isAboveQbiThreshold, /qbiHasPatronBusiness)) and /qbiHasPatronBusiness is a Count over ../isPatron — neither reads this fact, so opening this arm cannot re-route a patron to a different form. The contract that grew this rebody asked for that check and this is its answer: there is no second value-moving surface, only the one this fact already had. (c) An ABSENT collection is unchanged, because the arm is guarded on IsComplete(/qualifiedBusinesses) and falls through to the same Complete false the ~250 no-QBI cases resolve today.
THE PRINTED ADMISSION TEST'S FOURTH LIMB IS STILL UNREACHABLE AND IS NOT ABSORBED HERE. Form 8995's Note admits a filer who has "qualified business income from a qualified trade or business, real estate investment trust dividends, publicly traded partnership income, or a domestic production activities deduction passed through from an agricultural or horticultural cooperative". This fact is limb ONE. Limbs two and three are /isEntitledByReitOrPtp. Limb FOUR — a cooperative DPAD with no QBI and no REIT/PTP — has no route into this dictionary at all: Form 8995-A line 38 is reachable only through /qbiHasPatronBusiness, which counts patron items in /qualifiedBusinesses, so a filer with no business has no way to report one. The new arm does not change that and deliberately does not try to: a patron-flagged item is a /qualifiedBusinesses item and would travel this arm, but a DPAD-ONLY filer has no item to flag. AND THE REFUSAL IS CORRECT RATHER THAN MERELY UNBUILT: un-gating line 38 from item-presence is exactly the shape unit B forbade, because line 38 is the FAVOURABLE half of Schedule D and its gate is the same Part I line 1(e) checkbox that switches on the UNFAVOURABLE line-14 reduction. Serving limb four needs the Form 1099-PATR document intake, which is not built. Until then the population stays REFUSED (the $0 catch-all), never computed at a partial number.
WHY IT HAD TO BECOME ITS OWN FACT, which is the substantive decision of that rebody. The old /claimsQbiDeduction did TWO jobs with one expression: it answered the printed "Who Can Take the Deduction" test, and it suppressed the QBI of a trade or business the filer had disowned. Those jobs come apart the moment the gate becomes REIT-inclusive. Form 8995's test is a DISJUNCTION — "You have QBI, qualified REIT dividends, or qualified PTP income or loss" — so a REIT-only filer must pass the gate; but a filer who answered /hasQbiIncome=false AND holds a REIT must still have their business QBI suppressed, or an unrelated Form 1099-DIV would resurrect a deduction they had opted out of. Widening the gate alone would have shipped exactly that: on a return with an explicit /hasQbiIncome=false, 30,000 of entered QBI and 20,000 of box 5, the deduction would have gone from $0 to 10,000 where the printed form gives 4,000. So the SUPPRESSION moved with this fact and the ADMISSION stayed on the gate.
THREE CONSUMERS, and the two beyond the gate are the point. /claimsQbiDeduction reads it as one disjunct. taxCalculations:/qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction Case 1 reads it to gate the Form 8995 LINE 5 term, and /qbi8995aDeductionBeforeDpad reads it to gate the Form 8995-A LINE 27 term — the same fact on both sides of the section 199A threshold, so the business half cannot be suppressed on one side and not the other. Both of those guards are Switch(this → the component; else $0): line 1 / Part II lists QUALIFIED trades, businesses or aggregations, and a business the filer has declared not qualified does not go on it, so line 2 and line 4 are $0 and line 5 with them.
THE SHIPPING ARMS OF BOTH CONSUMERS NEED NO GUARD, and that is proved rather than assumed: /isEntitledByReitOrPtp implies /hasQualifiedReitOrPtpIntake (its answered-writable case can only be true when the writable IsComplete, which is the intake's own first disjunct, and its else-case IS the intake), so whenever the REIT/PTP limb opens the gate the REIT/PTP ARM of each consumer is the one selected. A shipping arm is therefore reached only when the gate was opened by THIS fact.
WHERE THE TWO DIVERGENCE WITNESSES ACTUALLY BITE, measured on a pre-fill run rather than reasoned from the tree, because the two paragraphs above make it easy to guess wrong. Both of those guards sit INSIDE their consumer's REIT/PTP arm. A return with no REIT and no PTP never takes that arm, so on such a return this fact moves nothing inside Form 8995 or Form 8995-A at all — it moves the OUTER gate /claimsQbiDeduction, and with it whether taxCalculations /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction selects a Case or falls to its $0 catch-all.
TYPE: Boolean, complete-safe false. BYTE-IDENTICAL AT INTRODUCTION: it resolves exactly what /claimsQbiDeduction resolved on all 938 committed cases, because no committed case reports any REIT or PTP amount by any route. THE COLLECTION ARM IS BYTE-IDENTICAL TOO, on the corpus scan recorded above rather than on expectation.

Fact.Name: Claims QBI deduction — Form 8995's "Who Can Take the Deduction" test, disjunctive
Fact.Description:
Complete-safe outer gate on Form 1040 line 13a: it is now the DISJUNCTION the printed form states, Any(/hasQualifiedTradeOrBusiness, /isEntitledByReitOrPtp, /qbiHasCooperativeDpad), where it used to be the first limb alone.
WHAT THE PRINTED FORM SAYS AND WHAT THE GRAPH USED TO DO. "Individuals and eligible estates and trusts that have QBI use Form 8995 to figure the QBI deduction if: • You have QBI, qualified REIT dividends, or qualified PTP income or loss (all defined later); and ..." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995.pdf, page 1, left column). Form 8995's own header states the same disjunction as a necessary condition: "You can claim the qualified business income deduction only if you have qualified business income from a qualified trade or business, real estate investment trust dividends, publicly traded partnership income, or a domestic production activities deduction passed through from an agricultural or horticultural cooperative" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8995.pdf, page 1). Until this rebody the gate was the FIRST limb only, so a filer whose sole §199A item was Form 1099-DIV box 5 or a publicly traded partnership's Schedule K-1 got $0 on line 13a no matter how large it was. That is the titled symptom of a known defect ("blocks the deduction for REIT/PTP-only filers"), and it is taxpayer-ADVERSE, which is why it is fixed rather than disclosed further.
WHY NOW AND NOT AT THE BOX-5 FILL. The gap was disclosed and left standing because its second limb had no computable body: /qualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss was not yet built, so a gate widened then would have admitted a population half of whose line 6 the graph could not compute. Both halves ship (box 5 via dividendReports:/section199ADividendsFromDividends, the PTP half via scheduleE:/formK1s item D plus box 20 code Z), so the limb is now a real fact and the gate can be honest.
THE SUPPRESSION DID NOT MOVE WITH THE ADMISSION, and that separation is the unit's real work. An explicit /hasQbiIncome=false means "this is not a qualified U.S. trade or business" and must keep meaning that: the printed disjunction makes the business question and the REIT/PTP question DIFFERENT questions, so an unrelated Form 1099-DIV may not answer the first one. The opt-out therefore lives on /hasQualifiedTradeOrBusiness and on the two component guards that fact feeds (Form 8995 line 5 in taxCalculations, Form 8995-A line 27 in /qbi8995aDeductionBeforeDpad) rather than on this gate. Without that move the naive widening would have paid a filer who disowned their business 20% of it anyway.
NOT THRESHOLD-CONDITIONAL, deliberately. Both limbs open this ONE gate, which both QBI paths read (taxCalculations Case 1's Form 8995 branch and Case 2's Form 8995-A branch), so the deduction cannot jump at the section 199A threshold — the "applied to only 1 of N QBI paths" shape a threshold-jump defect was refused for.
WHAT THIS GATE STILL DOES NOT REACH, disclosed rather than absorbed; neither is built. (1) An above-threshold REIT/PTP-only filer who never answers /writableClaims8995A: /qbiUsesForm8995A is false for them, so taxCalculations Case 2 does not fire and they take the $0 catch-all. Their gate is true and their deduction is $0 — unchanged from before this rebody, still taxpayer-adverse. If they DO opt in but leave /qualifiedBusinesses unanswered, /qbi8995aDpadPassThrough has no fallthrough and Form 1040 line 13a is Incomplete; that hole is pre-existing (a /hasQbiIncome=true filer in the same shape hits it today) and this rebody widens the door to it, not the hole itself. (2) The FOURTH limb of the printed header, a domestic production activities deduction passed through from a cooperative, is the third limb of this gate (/qbiHasCooperativeDpad): a filer whose only section 199A item is that deduction takes it on Form 8995-A line 38 through /qbiCooperativeDpadWithoutQualifiedBusiness.
TYPE/SIGN: Boolean, complete-safe false — unchanged by the rebody, which changed the body and not the surface. Both disjuncts are themselves complete-safe.

Fact.Name: This business's own share of its owner's deductible half of self-employment tax
Fact.Description:
THE PER-BUSINESS PRORATION. The portion of the deductible one-half self-employment tax (Schedule SE line 13) attributable to THIS Schedule C trade or business: its owner's line 13, times this business's own line 31, over that owner's Schedule SE line-3 base (his or her Schedule C total plus his or her K-1 box-14A earnings), floored at $0 and capped at that owner's whole line 13. A qbi-module fact living on scheduleC's collection, the same cross-module shape /filers/*/educatorExpenses uses.
WHY IT EXISTS, and it is a defect fix rather than a refactor. Until the Schedule C collection migration landed (loop-3) a return modeled exactly one Schedule C, so a return-level proration WAS a per-business one. It is not any more, and the return-level four-case Switch this replaces was measured wrong on the first shape the collection made expressible: on an MFJ return with a business on each spouse, its second case fired on the bare existential flag scheduleC:/scheduleCBelongsToSecondaryFiler and returned the SECONDARY's undivided line 13, so the PRIMARY's business contributed nothing at all to the QBI reduction. Direction of the old defect: taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, the direction the scope mandate treats as the worse one.
THE PRINTED RULE THIS IMPLEMENTS is a join between two forms stated at different granularities, and each half is printed. Section 199A is stated PER TRADE OR BUSINESS: the combined amount is "the sum of the amounts determined under paragraph (2) for each qualified trade or business carried on by the taxpayer" (IRC 199A(b)(1)(A)), QBI itself is the net amount of qualified items "with respect to any qualified trade or business of the taxpayer" (IRC 199A(c)(1)), and i8995 says in as many words that "if you're engaged in more than one trade or business, each trade or business is a separate trade or business for purposes of section 199A". Self-employment tax is stated PER INDIVIDUAL: each spouse files a separate Schedule SE and no part of one spouse's share may be included in figuring the other's net earnings. So the deductible half that i8995 tells us to net out of QBI is allocated inside ONE owner's own figures, across the businesses that produced that owner's own line-3 base.
BOTH OWNERSHIP CASES TEST OWNERSHIP, and the primary one says so explicitly rather than relying on the fall-through. The two per-item flags DO partition an answered, MFJ, complete return — but scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/belongsToSecondaryFiler declares two mid-interview states where it is Placeholder(false) rather than Complete, and in those an item that is in fact the spouse's matches NEITHER of the first two cases on a Complete value. A bare profit test on the primary's figures in case 3 would then charge HIS self-employment tax to HER trade — this cross-filer defect, reappearing one level below where the per-filer proration closed it, and measured at 134.00 on this unit's own witness with the guard removed. So case 3 carries ../belongsToPrimaryFiler and the final case is a true residual.
ZERO-DENOMINATOR PROOF, and it is a different proof from the one it replaces, which tested the owner's Schedule C total and box-14A subtotal SEPARATELY for positivity. This guard tests the SUM (that owner's Schedule C total plus that owner's box-14A) against $0 and divides only when it is strictly positive, so the divisor is never zero and never negative. It is strictly WEAKER on each term and strictly SUFFICIENT for the division, which is the point: the old pair of tests refused to prorate whenever either term was zero, which is how a single-business return with no K-1 fell through to the undivided line 13, and that fall-through is exactly what could not survive a second business.
THE FLOOR AND THE CEILING ARE BOTH LOAD-BEARING and neither comes from a printed rule; both are declared here as this dictionary's reading. FLOOR: a loss-making business gets $0 rather than a negative share. A negative attributable half-SE-tax would ADD to that business's QBI, and while it is arithmetically the exact inverse of the loss's effect on the owner's SE tax, no printed rule contemplates a negative "deductible part of self-employment tax attributable to the trade or business". CEILING: no business is attributed more than its owner's whole line 13. Without it the ratio is unbounded as the owner's net base approaches zero from above — a 50,000 business netted against a 49,000 loss in a second business would take fifty times the line 13 the return actually produced. CONSEQUENCE, stated rather than hidden: with a loss column present the shares can sum to slightly MORE than the owner's line 13, so the return-level total can over-reduce QBI. That is the taxpayer-UNFAVOURABLE direction and is the safe one to be wrong in; the exactly conservation-preserving alternative (signed shares, no floor) was REJECTED for the negative attribution it implies.
BYTE-IDENTICAL ON EVERY COMMITTED SINGLE-BUSINESS RETURN, which is what makes this landable as a correction rather than a rewrite: with one business and no working interest that business's line 31 IS its owner's whole Schedule C total, so the ratio is exactly 1 and the share is the undivided line 13 the old Case 2 / Case 4 returned; with one business and a K-1 of the owner's the ratio is the old Case 1 / Case 3 ratio unchanged.
SECTION 931/933: THE NUMERATOR IS NOW THE ITEM'S NONEXCLUDED LINE 31 (scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/netProfitSubjectToUsTax) AND THE DENOMINATOR IS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED. The denominator is the owner's Schedule SE line-3 base, which section 1402(a)(6) computes "without regard to section 933" and which therefore still contains the excluded income — that asymmetry IS Publication 570's fraction, expressed per item. With one owner, one business and no K-1 this resolves to line13 x nonexcluded / base, which is exactly scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentTaxDeduction's apportioned amount, so /qbiAutoDerivedAmount's minuend and subtrahend shrink by the same rule. With a K-1 in the base the item takes line13 x nonexcluded/base while the whole allowed deduction is line13 x (base-excluded)/base; the difference is the K-1's share of the allowed deduction, correctly not attributed to a Schedule C trade or business. THE MULTIPLICAND STAYS THE FULL PER-FILER LINE 13, and that is not an oversight: the fraction is already in the numerator, so apportioning the multiplicand as well would apply it twice. THE LesserOf CEILING IS NOW INERT RATHER THAN WRONG. It clamps at the owner's FULL line 13 while the numerator has shrunk, so it can only fail to bind; it is kept because it is what stops the clamp defect the prior body had, and that job is unchanged.
SIGN/TYPE: Dollar, never negative, never more than the owner's line 13, complete-safe $0 on every non-proration shape. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Deductible half-SE-tax attributable to the Schedule C trade or businesses
Fact.Description:
The portion of the deductible one-half self-employment tax (Schedule SE line 13) attributable to the Schedule C trade or business — now a SUM over the businesses rather than one return-level proration. Reduces QBI per i8995 (2025) p.2 / Reg. 1.199A-3(b)(1)(vi).
PER-BUSINESS. The arithmetic moved down onto /scheduleCs/*/qbiAttributableHalfSeTax, where the printed rule puts it, and what is left here is the aggregation this fact's consumer needs. The four-case return-level Switch that stood here (the per-filer proration) is in git history; it was correct while a return modeled exactly one Schedule C and became wrong the moment the collection migration made a second one expressible, because its second case fired on a BARE existential ownership flag and returned the secondary filer's undivided line 13 — first match wins, and the primary's business was never seen. The full defect analysis, its measured before-picture and the floor/ceiling reading are on the per-item fact above.
TWO TERMS, AND THE SECOND ONE IS NOT AN ITEM. Term one is the guarded CollectionSum over the entered businesses. Term two is the OIL AND GAS WORKING INTEREST's own share, computed the same way from the primary filer's figures: scheduleE:/workingInterestNetProfit is a trade or business reported on Schedule C, it is inside the combined line 31 that /qbiAutoDerivedAmount subtracts from, and it is deliberately NOT an item of /scheduleCs (it has no owner intake — see scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfit). A bare CollectionSum would therefore drop its half-SE-tax while keeping its profit, understating the reduction and OVERSTATING QBI: taxpayer-favourable, and a regression against the fall-through this fact used to have. It is attributed to the PRIMARY filer because that is the same back-compat default scheduleC:/primaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit already applies to the working interest itself. $0 on every committed scenario, none of which answers a working interest. THE WORKING INTEREST CARRIES NO SECTION 931/933 EXCLUSION AND IS CONSISTENT. It has no item of its own, so it has no place to record an exclusion — its whole profit therefore stays inside /qbiAutoDerivedAmount's minuend AND its whole share stays in this subtrahend. The pair is internally consistent, so the residual is not a QBI error; it is the same intake gap scheduleC:/scheduleCExcludedTerritoryNetProfit already discloses, in the same taxpayer-ADVERSE direction (territory income the filer cannot exclude).
THE DOUBLE GUARD ON TERM ONE IS THE MEASURED IDIOM, not style — the same IsComplete-then-CollectionSize wrapper scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfit and /qbiSimplifiedAmount use. /scheduleCs is UNANSWERED on most returns and a bare CollectionSum over an unanswered collection resolves PLACEHOLDER; this fact is Complete $0 on hundreds of committed scenarios and must stay that way.
THE ONE VALUE CLASS THAT MOVES, enumerated because it is the whole of this fact's corpus surface: a return with box-14A self-employment earnings and NO Schedule C at all. The old final True case handed the filer's entire line 13 to a Schedule C that does not exist; this body answers $0, because there is no trade or business for it to be attributable to. Three committed scenarios carry that shape, with this fact at 424.00, 2,120.00 and 780.00, and each moves to 0.00 with NOTHING downstream moving, since /scheduleCNetProfit is $0 on all three and /qbiAutoDerivedAmount's GreaterOf floor already produced $0 either way.
SIGN/TYPE: Dollar, never negative, complete-safe $0.

Fact.Name: Section 224 tips deducted, attributable to the Schedule C (excluded from QBI)
Fact.Description:
The amount deducted under IRC 224 for qualified tips that is attributable to this trade or business, and therefore must NOT be included in QBI: min(/qualifiedTipsDeduction, min(Schedule 1-A line 5, line 6)).
THE DEFECT THIS CLOSES. A Schedule C filer whose tips are part of gross receipts deducts them once on Schedule 1-A and, without this, keeps them in QBI as well — deducting the same dollars twice. i8995-A says plainly: "Do not include in QBI amounts that were deducted under IRC 224 for qualified tips."
BOTH BOUNDS ARE LOAD-BEARING. Bounding by /qualifiedTipsDeduction — the deduction ACTUALLY taken, after the 25,000 cap and the MAGI phaseout — means a filer whose deduction was capped or phased down loses only what they actually deducted. Bounding by line 5 means employee tips, which are reported on a W-2 and never enter Schedule C net profit, cannot reduce QBI. Line 5 is itself clamped at line 6 so a data-entry error cannot exclude more than the filer reported. Complete-safe: no tips answered ⇒ 0 ⇒ QBI unchanged, which is why this is additive.
DISCLOSED SCOPE GAP: when a filer has BOTH employee and trade-or-business tips AND the cap or phaseout binds, the deduction is attributed to the trade-or-business share FIRST. The instructions do not print an allocation rule and IRC 224 is too new to appear in any published US Code annual edition (the 2024 edition, the correct point-in-time text for TY2025, predates it), so no authority settles it. Attributing to the business first removes MORE from QBI, so it can only under-state the deduction, never over-state it. The REJECTED ALTERNATIVE is pro-rata allocation, which is equally unsupported and can under-remove.
"min(Schedule 1-A line 5, line 6)" ABOVE MEANS THE COMPUTED LINES. It used to mean the RAW writables schedule1A:/writableQualifiedTipsAmountTradeOrBusiness and schedule1A:/writableQualifiedTipsAmount, which was faithful while /qualifiedTipsDeduction itself ran off the raw typed total, and stopped being faithful when Schedule 1-A wired Part II. Two measured consequences, both now witnessed:
* A DETAIL-PATH RETURN WITH NO TYPED LINE 6 read $0 for the line-6 bound, so the whole LesserOf collapsed and NOTHING was carved out of QBI - the double deduction this fact exists to prevent, restored in full.
* WHERE THE SECTION 224(c) NET INCOME LIMIT CLAMPS LINE 5, the raw line-5 bound exceeded the business tips actually deducted, so QBI was cut by more than the deduction attributable to the business.
The sentence "Line 5 is itself clamped at line 6" now describes the graph as well as the intent. THE LINE 6 READ KEEPS AN IsComplete-GUARDED $0 DEFAULT: unlike the line 5 clamp, schedule1A:/schedule1ALine6QualifiedTips is NOT complete-safe (its fall-through arm reads the unanswered typed total), and reading it unguarded turned /qbiAutoDerivedAmount Incomplete on every return with no tips at all.
THE LINE 5 READ IS GUARDED TOO. The clamped line 5's net income limit subtracts scheduleSE:/fullSelfEmploymentTaxDeduction, which is Incomplete on a Schedule C return whose Schedule SE intake is unanswered. The operand is therefore read only when the trade-or-business tips intake (schedule1A:/writableQualifiedTipsAmountTradeOrBusiness) is complete, with $0 as the absent arm: a return that answers no trade-or-business tips reads $0, and a tips-answering return reads the computed, clamped line 5.

Fact.Name: Self-employed health insurance deduction attributable to Schedule C QBI
Fact.Description: The Schedule 1 line 17 self-employed health insurance deduction, but only when Form 7206 attributes the plan to a Schedule C business. A plan established under an S corporation, partnership, or farm does not reduce this Schedule C QBI subtotal. An exactly-one Schedule C plan-business attestation establishes the attribution directly; without an attestation, the existing single-profitable-business route is admitted only when its Form 7206 K-1 profit term is also zero. Complete-safe $0 when no attributable Schedule C deduction is established.

Fact.Name: Self-employed retirement plan deduction attributable to Schedule C QBI
Fact.Description: The part of the Schedule 1 line 16 deduction for self-employed SEP, SIMPLE and qualified plans that is attributable to the return's Schedule C trades or businesses: line 16 multiplied by the total net profit of the profitable Schedule C businesses (the oil or gas working interest included) and divided by the total net profit of every profitable self-employment trade or business on the return (Form 7206 line 5: Schedule C, Schedule F and Schedule K-1 box 14 code A). Losses are left out of both totals. With one profitable Schedule C and no other self-employment profit this is the whole line 16 amount. The share attributable to a farm or a partnership reduces that business's own qualified business income, which the filer enters, and is not taken here. Complete-safe: $0 when line 16 is $0 or unanswered, or when no self-employment trade or business shows a profit.

Fact.Name: Auto-derived below-threshold QBI (Schedule C)
Fact.Description:
Qualified business income derived from the Schedule C net profit reduced by the deductible half of self-employment tax, the self-employed health insurance deduction and the self-employed retirement plan deduction attributable to it, floored at zero. Used as the QBI amount for the below-threshold Form 8995 simplified deduction when the taxpayer did not enter a list of qualified businesses at /qualifiedBusinesses. Does not include K-1 box-14A SE earnings (see the block comment above).
SECTION 931/933: BOTH HALVES MOVED, TOGETHER. The minuend is now scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax and the subtrahend's per-item numerators are each business's own nonexcluded line 31, so a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico no longer takes a Qualified Business Income Deduction on income they exclude under section 933 ("Bona fide residents of Puerto Rico cannot take the Qualified Business Income Deduction related to their Puerto Rico source self-employment income they are excluding under Sec. 933", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p1321.pdf, page 6). Moving either alone was refused and the reason is on scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax: minuend-only understates QBI, subtrahend-only denies a deduction on income still reported as taxable. Value-identical on every return that excludes nothing, which is every committed case.
THE ABOVE-THRESHOLD TWIN MOVED IN THE SAME COMMIT. /qualifiedBusinesses/*/scheduleCDerivedQbi is this fact one grain down; moving one and not the other would make the section 199A deduction JUMP at the threshold for this population.
⚠⚠ THE INCOME SIDE HAS NOT MOVED, SO THIS CUT LANDS ON INCOME THE RETURN STILL TAXES. income:/totalIncome still reads scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfit, the COMBINED line 31 — this cut does not touch income.xml, and the seven-consumer deferral list is on scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax. So a filer who answers the per-item exclusion intake is taxed on the excluded profit AND loses the Qualified Business Income Deduction on it. DIRECTION: COMPOUNDING TAXPAYER-ADVERSE — the safer class, with precedent under the same condition (this standard-deduction proration, this QBI admission gate, both while total income still carries the excluded profit), but not a rounding residual. NOT DETECTED BY ctcOdc:/knockoutPossessionOrPuertoRicoIncomeExclusion's condition (v), which fires on the UNANSWERED intake while this is the ANSWERED case. It discharges when income:/totalIncome moves. Fact.Name: Qualified publicly traded partnership income or (loss) — the PTP half of Form 8995 line 6
Fact.Description:
The PTP half of Form 8995 line 6 / Form 8995-A line 28, as a section 199A quantity: scheduleE:/k1QualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss, the sum over the Schedule K-1s whose item D ("Check if this is a publicly traded partnership (PTP)") is checked of the box 20 code Z qualified PTP amount each reports.
WHY IT IS A PASS-THROUGH AND NOT A BODY. The contract for this node said its "real home is a Schedule K-1 intake" and that "the module file is not a claim about where the fact belongs", and the intake duly landed in dictionary/ty2025/scheduleE.xml, where /formK1s lives. The section 199A SIDE of the story is this module's, though: what a qualified PTP amount is FOR, which arm it selects, and how it composes with the REIT half are all decided here. So the path the contract named ships here, one dependency deep, and the collection arithmetic ships beside the collection. Nothing else reads the scheduleE aggregate.
SIGN: MAY BE NEGATIVE, no floor and no rounding at this node. "Line 6. Enter income as a positive number and losses as a negative number", and the floor is line 8 / line 30 inside each consumer, so a qualified PTP loss stops at the REIT/PTP subtotal and never reduces the line-5 / line-27 QBI component.
COMPOSES WITH THE REIT HALF, NOT BESIDE IT, which is what IRC 199A(b)(1)(B) requires: the combined amount takes "20 percent of the aggregate amount of the qualified REIT dividends and qualified" publicly traded partnership income. ONE printed line, one component, one 20%. THE QUOTE STOPS WHERE THE CITED SPAN STOPS, deliberately: lines 86-87 end mid-sentence because line 88 is a page header, and dividendReports:/section199ADividendsFromDividends already records that one-line-too-far trap for this file. The continuation, on the other side of the header, is "publicly traded partnership income of the taxpayer for the taxable year" (26 U.S.C. 199A, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section199A&num=0&edition=2024, the extraction's right column). /qualifiedReitDividendsAndPtpIncome ADDS this to the Form 1099-DIV box-5 total in its documentary arm; it does not give the PTP half a component of its own.
It is rebodied for the SSTB-PTP fill (see /sstbPtpQualifiedAmountAfterApplicablePercentage). On every return that never holds an above-threshold SSTB PTP the new first arm's gate is false and the second arm reproduces the old body verbatim — no value moves on the existing corpus, proven rather than merely argued (PREDICTED_DELTA, AUTHORED phase notes).

Fact.Name: The filer reported a Form 8995 line 6 / Form 8995-A line 28 amount by SOME route
Fact.Description:
The REIT/PTP arm gate, factored out so ONE fact holds it for BOTH consumers. True when the filer reported a line-6 / line-28 amount by any of the three routes that exist: (1) the return-level combined writable is ANSWERED (/writableQualifiedReitDividendsAndPtpIncome, the taxpayer override); (2) the Form 1099-DIV box-5 total is above $0 (dividendReports:/section199ADividendsFromDividends); (3) a Schedule K-1 reports a qualified PTP amount (scheduleE:/hasK1QualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss).
WHY IT IS A FACT AND NOT AN INLINE Any(), and this is the shape the fill's contract required rather than a tidiness preference. The disjunction used to be written TWICE — once inline in taxCalculations:/qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction Case 1 and once here at /qbi8995aDeductionBeforeDpad — and the two copies had to be widened together every time a new route to line 6 landed. That is the "applied to only 1 of N QBI paths" defect waiting to happen: a filer's threshold position is a continuous function of income, so a gate widened on one side alone makes the deduction JUMP at the section 199A threshold for a reason no printed form describes. One fact, both consumers, and the next route to line 6 is a one-line change here.
THE THIRD DISJUNCT IS AN EXISTENCE TEST, NOT A MAGNITUDE TEST, and the asymmetry with the second is deliberate. Box 5 carries Min $0 per payer, so a $0 total contributes nothing to line 8 and `> $0` is both correct and byte-identical there. Qualified PTP income MAY BE NEGATIVE, so a qualified PTP LOSS has to select the arm too — on a magnitude test a filer with a PTP loss and a prior-year carryforward would take the preserved arm and silently lose the carryforward, which is exactly the failure /qualifiedReitPtpLossCarryforwardIn's Description predicted for this fill.
BYTE-IDENTICAL AT INTRODUCTION: with no /formK1s item answering a PTP amount, disjunct (3) is false on every committed return and this fact resolves exactly what the two inline copies resolved.

Fact.Name: Who Can Take the Deduction, second limb — the filer has qualified REIT dividends or qualified PTP income or (loss)
Fact.Description:
THE SECOND LIMB of Form 8995's disjunctive admission test, and the other half of the /claimsQbiDeduction rebody. True when the filer HAS qualified REIT dividends or qualified PTP income or loss — "You have QBI, qualified REIT dividends, or qualified PTP income or loss (all defined later)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995.pdf, page 1).
IT IS NOT /hasQualifiedReitOrPtpIntake, AND IT DELEGATES TO IT — both halves of that sentence are deliberate, because the obvious move was to wire the gate straight to the fact the PTP fill had already factored. ENTITLEMENT AND INTAKE ARE DIFFERENT QUESTIONS. /hasQualifiedReitOrPtpIntake asks "did the filer report a line-6 entry by SOME route", and it must answer TRUE to an answered $0 return-level writable, because that answered zero is precisely what wins over the Form 1099-DIV box-5 default (the adjudicated row in scripts/answered_zero_allowlist.txt). This fact asks the PRINTED question, and a filer who has just stated that their combined qualified REIT dividends and qualified PTP amount is zero does not "have" any. So the two facts part in exactly one place — an ANSWERED $0 writable — and nowhere else. The difference is value-inert (line 6 is $0, line 8 floors to $0, line 9 is $0), so what it buys is an honest gate flag rather than a dollar.
THE ROUTE LIST IS NOT REPEATED HERE, and that is the reason for the Switch rather than a second three-way Any(). The else-case IS /hasQualifiedReitOrPtpIntake, so the three routes to line 6 — the return-level writable, the box-5 total, a Schedule K-1 with item D checked — are enumerated in ONE place and a fourth route added there is inherited by this fact with no edit. Writing the disjunction twice is the shape the PTP fill's contract refused and the shape this factoring exists to make unrepresentable.
WHY THE GUARD IS AN IsComplete SWITCH AND NOT All(IsComplete(w), NotEqual(w, $0)). A bare comparison against an UNANSWERED writable resolves Incomplete, and this fact is read by the outer gate on every return in the corpus — an Incomplete here would blank Form 1040 line 13a corpus-wide. The Switch evaluates the writable only inside the case that has already proved it answered, which is the same unanswered-safety shape /qualifiedReitDividendsAndPtpIncome uses one fact above and for the same reason.
EXISTENCE ON THE PTP ROUTE, MAGNITUDE ON THE BOX-5 ROUTE — inherited from /hasQualifiedReitOrPtpIntake and correct for this question too, which is worth re-deriving rather than assuming. The printed limb reads "qualified PTP income OR LOSS", so a PTP loss satisfies it; a magnitude test would shut the gate on a loss year and, on a return carrying a line-7 prior-year carryforward, discard it silently. Box 5 carries a Min $0 per payer, so a $0 total is indistinguishable from no REIT dividends at all and the strict > $0 there is both correct and byte-identical. ONE INHERITED EDGE, disclosed: a Schedule K-1 with item D checked reporting a qualified PTP amount of exactly $0 selects the limb through the intake's existence test. That is value-inert for the same reason the answered-$0 writable is, and it is left as the intake fact defines it rather than special-cased here.
TYPE: Boolean, complete-safe false. BYTE-IDENTICAL AT INTRODUCTION: false on all 938 committed cases, because none of them reports a REIT or PTP amount by any route — the same measurement that makes the whole rebody corpus-neutral.

Fact.Name: Qualified REIT dividends and PTP income or (loss)
Fact.Description:
Form 8995 line 6 / Form 8995-A line 28. Complete-safe: $0 when the taxpayer answered neither intake, so every return without REIT dividends or PTP income is byte-identical to the pre-fill graph (line 8/line 30 floors at zero, line 9/line 31 is $0, line 10/line 32 equals line 5/line 27).
THERE ARE TWO INTAKES AND THIS FACT PICKS BETWEEN THEM. dividendReports:/section199ADividendsFromDividends is the DOCUMENTARY total — Form 1099-DIV box 5, "Section 199A dividends", summed across payers — and it is the default source. /writableQualifiedReitDividendsAndPtpIncome is now the TAXPAYER OVERRIDE, taken whenever it is answered. That is the /rentalProperties/*/depreciationExpense precedence idiom, not a sum, and the choice between them is the substantive decision of this fill:
* OVERRIDE, NOT SUM, because the writable is the WHOLE of line 6, not a residual. It was authored as "ONE printed entry combining two real-world sources" and every scenario and node test that answers it enters the COMBINED figure. Adding box 5 to it would DOUBLE-COUNT the REIT half for exactly the filer who did what the intake asked. * The writable does not retire, because a taxpayer override over a documentary default is worth keeping in its own right — but it is no longer the only route to the PTP half. THIS BULLET IS THE CORRECTED VERSION of one that said it was ("it is still the only route for the half box 5 cannot carry: qualified PTP income or (loss), /qualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss"). * The cost, stated rather than hidden: a filer who answers the combined writable with a PTP-only figure while also entering box 5 loses the box-5 amount. That is a prompt-level hazard (the question must ask for the COMBINED total), not a graph-level one, and it is now AVOIDABLE rather than structural — with both documents entered the derivation is complete and no manual answer is needed at all.
AN ANSWERED $0 WRITABLE WINS, AND THAT IS ADJUDICATED, NOT ACCIDENTAL. The guard is a bare IsComplete, which is the answered-zero shape lint_answered_zero flags; the row "/qualifiedReitDividendsAndPtpIncome::/writableQualifiedReitDividendsAndPtpIncome" in scripts/answered_zero_allowlist.txt records the adjudication and this paragraph is its reasoning. The blessed strict-GreaterThan guard is UNAVAILABLE HERE, and refusing it is a correctness decision rather than a style one: line 6 is signed by instruction ("Enter income as a positive number and losses as a negative number"), so a `> $0` guard would fall through to the box-5 total for every answered NEGATIVE line 6 and silently delete a filer's qualified PTP LOSS — a strictly worse defect than the answered-zero shadow it would prevent. A `$0` answer is a deliberate "my combined REIT and PTP amount is zero", the same class of deliberate answer as an answered-$0 depreciation override.
MAY BE NEGATIVE — this fact passes an answered sign through unchanged, floor and all: the floor is line 8's / line 30's, not this node's, and it is applied inside each consumer so that a REIT/PTP loss never reduces the QBI component. The documentary arm cannot be negative (box 5 carries Min $0 per payer). The two consumers are the whole point of the single path: taxCalculations /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction Case 1 (below the section 199A threshold, Form 8995 lines 6-10) and /qbi8995aDeductionBeforeDpad (above it, Form 8995-A lines 28-32). They read ONE path so the component cannot be applied to one QBI path and not the other. A THIRD consumer reads it UNGATED — /qualifiedReitPtpLossCarryforwardToNextYear — so a box-5 amount now reaches the carry-OUT as well.
ROUNDING: the documentary arm is Round(box 5 total + qualified PTP income or (loss)), one Round on the printed line ("include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 23); the box 5 total arrives unrounded. An answered writable is taken as entered.

Fact.Name: Qualified REIT dividends and PTP (loss) carryforward TO next year (carry-OUT)
Fact.Description:
The carry-OUT half of the cross-year pair whose carry-IN half is /qualifiedReitPtpLossCarryforwardIn above. 2025 Instructions for Form 8995, "Line 8": "Any negative amount will be carried forward to the next year. This carryforward doesn't affect the deductibility of the loss for purposes of any other provisions of the Code" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995.pdf, page 4, right column).
IT IS EXACTLY WHAT THE FLOOR DISCARDS. Form 8995 line 8 and Form 8995-A line 30 combine the current-year REIT/PTP amount with the prior-year carryforward and then floor the result at zero ("If zero or less, enter -0-" / "If less than zero, enter -0-"). This fact is the magnitude of that discarded negative part, and nothing else: it is the same subtraction both consumers perform, kept when it goes below zero instead of thrown away. Both consumers compute an IDENTICAL pre-floor combine — taxCalculations /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction Case 1 and /qbi8995aDeduction each build Subtract(/qualifiedReitDividendsAndPtpIncome, /qualifiedReitPtpLossCarryforwardIn) inside a GreaterOf against $0 — so ONE node serves both section 199A branches and the carry-OUT cannot jump at the threshold, which is the same reason the carry-IN is one node.
STORED AS A POSITIVE MAGNITUDE, and the round-trip is the reason. Whatever this fact holds must be answerable DIRECTLY into next year's /writableQualifiedReitPtpLossCarryforwardFromPriorTaxYear, which carries Min $0 and is subtracted by both consumers. Storing the signed negative the form prints would put a sign flip between the two halves of a pair whose whole purpose is to line up, and a filer copying the number forward would be refused by that Min $0 limit. So the pair shares one convention end to end: magnitude out, magnitude in, subtract at the consumer.
DIRECTION AND SAFETY: value-NEUTRAL in this tax year. No current-year fact reads it, so it cannot move any return's tax, and the corpus is byte-identical. Its exposure is entirely in the following year — under-stating it would cost the filer a carryforward they are entitled to. It is NOT transmitted; see the Export note below.
IT READS THE LINE-6 INTAKE UNGATED, and that mattered the moment the intake gained a second source. Neither consumer's arm-selection Switch reaches this fact — it is a standalone derived node over two complete-safe aliases — so when /dividendReports/*/section199ADividends landed and /qualifiedReitDividendsAndPtpIncome began defaulting to the Form 1099-DIV box-5 total, THIS fact started moving for filers who answered no writable at all.
WHY IT IS EXPORTED RATHER THAN WIRED, and why this is not an orphan. Its consumer is next year's Form 8995 line 7 / Form 8995-A line 29 — a real consumer in a real return, just not this one. <Export downstreamFacts="true"/> is the same channel its carry-IN sibling uses and is deliberately NOT mef="true" — but NOT for the reason this paragraph used to give. It said "no line of the 2025 return carries this number", and that is simply FALSE: BOTH forms print this carry-out as their last line. Form 8995 line 17 is "Total qualified REIT dividends and PTP (loss) carryforward. Combine lines 6 and 7. If greater than zero, enter -0-" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8995.pdf, page 1) and Form 8995-A line 40 is the same quantity worded for that form, "Combine lines 28 and 29. If zero or greater, enter -0-" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8995a.pdf, page 2). Both are printed inside parentheses, like their line 7 / line 29 carry-IN counterparts.
THE TRUE REASON, re-decided on that corrected premise, is the repo's MeF surface rather than the form's: NOTHING in this module is mef-exported. The whole QBI chain reaches MeF through exactly one fact, taxCalculations:/qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction (Form 1040 line 13), which is also the only QBI row in dictionary/manifest/spine-registry.tsv. Not one Form 8995 or Form 8995-A line-level fact carries mef="true" — not line 15, not line 37, not line 39 — so tagging line 17 / line 40 would make this the single transmitted line of a form whose every other line is untransmitted, an inconsistency invariant #7 (MeF is not this repo's surface) says to resolve by leaving it alone rather than by widening. The omission stands; only its justification changes.
RENEGOTIATED — THE CONTRACT'S "CROSS-YEAR PLUMBING UNIT" PREMISE DID NOT SURVIVE. The fill for this node is cross-year plumbing, and it comes together with scheduleD's two capital-loss carry-OUTs and scheduleA's charitable one. The absent mechanism is real, but it is not THIS node's next level — it is the next level of the cross-year PAIR, and the pair already runs on the attested carry-IN in the meantime. This fact reads only current-year facts (the REIT/PTP amount and the attested carry-IN) and produces an informational output: no prior-year state is READ. Nothing about the three sibling carry-OUTs makes them prerequisites — each is computable from its own module's current-year facts, and bundling four modules into one unit would couple reviews that share only a deferred mechanism neither needs. What the contract was right about is that an attested single-year carry-IN is an interim shape; this fact is the half that makes the pair checkable at all.
SIBLING, NOT DUPLICATE, of the section 199A(c)(2) qualified-business-loss carryforward (Form 8995 line 16 / Schedule C (Form 8995-A) line 6). Line 16 carries the QBI loss; this line carries the REIT/PTP loss. Different subtotals, different lines. BOTH HALVES OF THAT SIBLING PAIR NOW SHIP — the sentence this replaces said "which still has NEITHER half built", which was already stale when the carry-IN landed and is doubly so now that /qualifiedBusinessNetLossCarryforwardToNextYear landed the same day, built on this fact's own precedent.

Fact.Name: Taxable income before QBI deduction
Fact.Description: Form 8995 Line 11: AGI minus standard-or-itemized deductions (Form 1040 line 12e) minus Schedule 1-A additional deductions (line 13b), without the QBI deduction itself (line 13a). Used as the income base for the 20% cap to avoid a circular dependency.

Fact.Name: QBI threshold non-MFJ
Fact.Description: TY2025 taxable-income threshold for Form 8995 simplified computation, for all filers other than MFJ. Above this threshold, Form 8995-A is required.

Fact.Name: QBI threshold MFJ
Fact.Description: TY2025 taxable-income threshold for Form 8995 simplified computation, for married filing jointly filers. Above this threshold, Form 8995-A is required.

Fact.Name: Is above QBI threshold
Fact.Description: True if taxable income before the QBI deduction exceeds the applicable threshold. When true, Form 8995-A is required — the simplified Form 8995 does not apply.

Fact.Name: Completing Form 8995-A
Fact.Description: Whether the taxpayer is completing Form 8995-A because taxable income is above the threshold and they have provided the per-business W-2 wage / UBIA / SSTB detail. Gate for the above-threshold path; complete-safe false when unanswered, so an above-threshold return that has NOT provided Form 8995-A detail keeps a $0 deduction (never over-deducts).

Fact.Name: Claims Form 8995-A deduction
Fact.Description: Complete-safe gate for the above-threshold Form 8995-A path: true only when /writableClaims8995A is answered and true. Resolves Complete false when unanswered, so an above-threshold return without Form 8995-A detail resolves a $0 deduction (World-1 safe).

Fact.Name: This return works Form 8995-A rather than the simplified Form 8995
Fact.Description:
THE FORM-SELECTION GATE. True when the filer has supplied the Form 8995-A per-business detail (/claims8995A) AND at least one of the two INDEPENDENT reasons the printed authorities give for being on that form: taxable income above the section 199A threshold, or conducting a trade or business with a specified agricultural or horticultural cooperative (/qbiHasPatronBusiness).
WHY THE PATRON DISJUNCT IS NOT OPTIONAL. Form 8995's own header states its admission test CONJUNCTIVELY: "Use this form if your taxable income, before your qualified business income deduction, is at or below $197,300 ($394,600 if married filing jointly), and you aren't a patron of an agricultural or horticultural cooperative" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8995.pdf, page 1). The Form 8995-A instructions state the mirror image as a DISJUNCTION: "Individuals and eligible estates and trusts use Form 8995-A to figure the QBI deduction if: ... Your 2025 taxable income before your QBI deduction is more than $394,600 married filing jointly, and $197,300 for all other returns; or You're a patron in a specified agricultural or horticultural cooperative" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 1, with "Otherwise, use Form 8995" at line 58). Until this fact landed, taxCalculations /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction selected its Form 8995 arm on the THRESHOLD ALONE, so a below-threshold patron was routed to the one form whose header excludes them and their Form 1040 line 13 saw NEITHER the line-14 patron reduction NOR the line-38 DPAD.
THE /claims8995A CONJUNCT IS KEPT, AND IT IS THIS UNIT'S DISCLOSED LIMIT. Form 8995-A is modeled as an OPT-IN — the whole per-business ladder (/qualifiedBusinesses/*/effectiveQbi and below) resolves only when /claims8995A is true — so this fact reads "the filer is on Form 8995-A and the graph holds the detail to work it", NOT "the filer is required to be on Form 8995-A". The obvious-looking alternative Any(/claims8995A, /qbiHasPatronBusiness) is WRONG and would be a regression, not a wider fix: a patron who never opted in has no Form 8995-A ladder at all, so routing them to it would make /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction INCOMPLETE and blank Form 1040 line 13, which is worse than today's wrong-but-resolved number. The residual — a below-threshold patron who never answers /writableClaims8995A — keeps the Form 8995 arm.
WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO: it does not replace /claims8995A anywhere in the ladder. Every fact gated on /claims8995A today stays gated on /claims8995A, because every population this fact routes to Form 8995-A has /claims8995A true by construction (it is a conjunct), so a swap would only change which returns the ladder resolves ON, not what it computes.
CONSUMERS: taxCalculations /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction (which form the deduction comes from) and /qualifiedBusinesses/*/qbiComponent (the Form 8995-A line 3 "skip lines 4 through 12" arm, which is scoped to filers actually on that form). TYPE: Boolean, complete-safe false — both conjuncts are themselves complete-safe.

Fact.Name: QBI threshold (applicable to filing status)
Fact.Description: The taxable-income threshold applicable to the taxpayer's filing status: $394,600 MFJ, else $197,300. Form 8995-A / Schedule A line "Threshold".

Fact.Name: QBI phase-in range width
Fact.Description: Width of the phase-in range above the threshold: $100,000 MFJ, else $50,000.

Fact.Name: QBI upper threshold (top of phase-in range)
Fact.Description: Threshold plus the phase-in range width: $494,600 MFJ, else $247,300. At or below this the wage/UBIA cap and SSTB reduction phase in; above it they apply fully.

Fact.Name: Is above QBI upper threshold
Fact.Description: True if taxable income before the QBI deduction exceeds the upper threshold (top of the phase-in range). When true, the wage/UBIA limitation applies fully and an SSTB is fully excluded.

Fact.Name: Is in QBI phase-in range
Fact.Description: True if taxable income before the QBI deduction is above the threshold but not above the upper threshold. In this band the wage/UBIA limitation and SSTB reduction phase in ratably.

Fact.Name: Qualified trades, businesses, or aggregations
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's qualified trades, businesses, or aggregations — one item per row of Form 8995-A Part I ("Trade, Business, or Aggregation Information", rows A/B/C plus "Attach additional worksheets when needed") and per row of Form 8995 line 1 (rows i-v). The instructions confirm the count is unbounded: "If you have four or more trades or businesses, attach a statement with the information for Parts I, II, and III, as applicable" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 6, right column).
A NEW COLLECTION RATHER THAN A REUSE, and the alternatives were checked rather than assumed. /formK1s carries no section 199A field at all (no box-20 code Z, no W-2 wages, no UBIA, no SSTB flag), ONE K-1 can report SEVERAL trades or businesses on its section 199A statement, and it excludes sole proprietorships and rental enterprises entirely. /rentalProperties is one item per Schedule E Part I property, which is the wrong grain in both directions — a section 199A rental enterprise may aggregate several properties under the Rev. Proc. 2019-38 safe harbor, and a property may fail to be a trade or business at all. Schedule C is not a collection at all today. So the grain the form prints has no existing home.

Fact.Name: Qualified business income or (loss) for this trade, business, or aggregation
Fact.Description:
Form 8995-A line 2, "Qualified business income from the trade, business, or aggregation", and Form 8995 line 1 column (c), "Qualified business income or (loss)". The per-item successor of the retired return-level /writableQualifiedBusinessIncomeAmount.
SIGN — MAY BE NEGATIVE, and deliberately carries NO Min $0 limit: column (c) is printed as "income or (loss)" and Form 8995 line 2 combines the rows, so netting a loss in one business against income in another is the arithmetic the form asks for. The floor is downstream, at Form 8995 line 4 ("Combine lines 2 and 3. If zero or less, enter -0-"), which is already built. The §199A(c)(2) qualified-business-loss carryforward (Form 8995 line 3 / Form 8995-A Schedule C) is modeled — this sentence used to end "is still unmodeled — the engine has no multi-year state". The engine still holds no multi-year state: the carry-IN is an ATTESTED writable the filer states (/writableQualifiedBusinessNetLossCarryforwardFromPriorTaxYear) and the carry-OUT (/qualifiedBusinessNetLossCarryforwardToNextYear) is computed from this return alone, which is the cross-year shape rather than a exception.

Fact.Name: Which Schedule C this trade, business, or aggregation is
Fact.Description:
The /scheduleCs item that reports THIS section 199A qualified trade or business, when the business is a sole proprietorship the return already files a Schedule C for. OPTIONAL and deliberately un-Placeholdered: a qualified trade or business may equally be a K-1 trade or a rental enterprise with no Schedule C at all (the reason /qualifiedBusinesses is its own collection rather than a reuse), so an unanswered link is a legitimate and common state and NOT a defect.
WHAT THE LINK BUYS, and it is exactly one thing: it lets the Schedule C auto-derivation be attributed to a BUSINESS instead of to the RETURN. Before it, /qbiSimplifiedAmount could only fall back to a return-level /qbiAutoDerivedAmount when the whole collection was absent or empty, and Form 8995-A's per-column ladder could not reach the derivation at all. See ../scheduleCDerivedQbi below for the arithmetic and ../scheduleCLinkResolves for the guard that makes an unanswered business still refusable.
NO PLACEHOLDER, deliberately, and this is the load-bearing difference from scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/filer, which DOES default to the primary filer. That fact's default is back-compat for an attribution every return already had; this one's default would INVENT an attribution — "the first Schedule C is this business's" — and the whole point of the guard below is that an un-established link must not silently supply $0. A Placeholder here would re-open the very compute-wrong this unit exists to close.
NO CONSISTENCY GUARD ON THE TARGET'S OWNER. A link may name a Schedule C owned by either spouse and nothing here checks that against anything, because section 199A has no per-individual grain to check against: the deduction is computed on the joint return's taxable income and Form 8995-A Part I has no taxpayer column. The half-SE-tax term the derivation subtracts IS per-individual and resolves that inside /scheduleCs/*/qbiAttributableHalfSeTax, on the linked business's own owner, so the join already lands on the right person's Schedule SE without a guard here.
TWO ITEMS MAY NAME THE SAME SCHEDULE C, AND THE GRAPH REFUSES THEM EXACTLY. Two /qualifiedBusinesses items that both leave their QBI unanswered and both link to one /scheduleCs item each derive that Schedule C's whole amount, so the return double-counts; direction taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, which is the worse one. The refusal is not written HERE, and that is a placement choice rather than a limitation: the test needs one fixed value every link can be compared against, so it lives on the TARGET collection as /scheduleCs/*/qbiIsDuplicatedAttributionTarget, whose enclosing item IS that value. The return-level consumer is /qbiHasDuplicateScheduleCAttribution. No operator binds an outer item inside a Filter, but that does not make the test unreachable - the Descriptions of both facts named above carry the reasoning and its engine citations.
ONE CLASS IS STILL ADMITTED, AND DELIBERATELY: two businesses sharing one Schedule C while at least one of them ANSWERS its own QBI amount. That double count predates this link — a filer could always enter one business twice and type the number in both columns — and it is VISIBLE rather than derived, so it is not what the derivation made silent.

Fact.Name: Allocable share of W-2 wages for this trade, business, or aggregation
Fact.Description: Form 8995-A line 4, "Allocable share of W-2 wages from the trade, business, or aggregation". Used only in the above-threshold W-2 wage / UBIA limitation. The per-item successor of the retired return-level /writableQbiW2Wages.

Fact.Name: Allocable share of UBIA of qualified property for this trade, business, or aggregation
Fact.Description: Form 8995-A line 7, "Allocable share of the unadjusted basis immediately after acquisition (UBIA) of all qualified property". Used only in the above-threshold limitation. The per-item successor of the retired return-level /writableQbiUbia.

Fact.Name: This trade or business is a specified service trade or business
Fact.Description: Form 8995-A Part I line 1 column (b), "Check if specified service". PER-BUSINESS, which is the defect the migration closes: the retired return-level /writableQbiIsSstb was one flag for the whole return, so a filer with an SSTB and a non-SSTB business got the applicable-percentage haircut applied to both or to neither. Above the upper threshold an SSTB gets no QBI deduction; within the phase-in range it is reduced by the applicable percentage. Complete-safe false when unanswered, via /qualifiedBusinesses/*/isSstb.

Fact.Name: This line 1 row is an AGGREGATION of several trades or businesses, not a single one
Fact.Description:
Form 8995-A Part I line 1 column (c), "Check if aggregation" — the column between the SSTB checkbox and the TIN, and the last of the four line 1 flags this collection had not landed. The instruction is explicit about what checking it means for the rest of the row: "If you aggregated multiple trades or businesses into a single business on Schedule B (Form 8995-A), enter the aggregation group name, for example, Aggregation 1, 2, 3, etc., instead of entering the business name, check the box under line 1(c), and leave line 1(d) blank" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 6, RIGHT column).
IT MOVES NO NUMBER, AND THAT IS THE POINT RATHER THAN A LIMITATION. An aggregation is ONE Part I column, so lines 2 through 15 are worked on it exactly as they are for a single trade or business, and line 16 sums the columns either way. What the filer enters in an aggregation row is already combined: "You must combine the QBI, W-2 wages, and UBIA of qualified property for all aggregated trades or businesses, for purposes of applying the W-2 wage and UBIA of qualified property limitations" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 3, LEFT column). So ../writableQualifiedBusinessIncome, ../writableW2Wages and ../writableUbia carry the combined amounts and every downstream fact is unchanged. This flag records WHICH KIND of row the item is; no AMOUNT computes from it, which is why its complete-safe view carries an Export as well as a consumer.
WHY IT LANDS ANYWAY. Without it the graph cannot distinguish an aggregation row from a single-business row at all, and that distinction is the only part of the Schedule B election this dictionary can hold: Schedule B's own content is the per-aggregation MEMBER LIST, a collection nested inside a collection item, which has no expressible home here. Landing the checkbox alone is not a partial computation — there is no computation to be partial about.
IT IS NO LONGER THE ELECTION'S ENTIRE FOOTPRINT. the election's printed ELIGIBILITY requirements are per-aggregation scalar data, expressible with no member list and no nested collection, and they now ship as ../writableAggregationOwnershipTestMet and ../writableAggregationFactorsTestMet with the refusal at ../hasIneligibleAggregation. What remains out of this repo is the Schedule B DISCLOSURE attachment alone.
TYPE: Boolean, writable. Complete-safe false via ../isAggregation. UNCHECKED IS THE CONSERVATIVE DEFAULT and is also the printed default: not aggregating is what a filer who never opens Schedule B does, and aggregating pools W-2 wages and UBIA across the group, so a row wrongly left unchecked UNDER-claims rather than over-claims.

Fact.Name: Every trade or business in this aggregation meets the 50% common-ownership and common-year-end test
Fact.Description:
Requirement 1 of the Form 8995-A aggregation election, answered per aggregation row: "You or a group of persons directly or indirectly own 50% or more of each trade or business for a majority of the tax year, including the last day of the tax year, and all trades or businesses use the same tax year end" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 3, LEFT column).
WHY IT IS A NEW ANSWER RATHER THAN A DERIVATION. Nothing this dictionary holds knows who owns a trade or business, what fraction, for how much of the year, or what year end it uses. Every term of the requirement is outside the return's arithmetic, so the only honest model is an attestation. It is PER-ITEM because the election is per-row: Part I line 1 tells an aggregating filer to name the row "Aggregation 1, 2, 3, etc." and check the box under line 1(c) (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 6, RIGHT column), and a return may carry an aggregation row beside ordinary single-business rows.
IT IS READ ONLY ON AN AGGREGATION ROW. ../hasIneligibleAggregation asks for it only when ../isAggregation is true, so a filer who never aggregates is never asked and is never refused over it. Complete-safe FALSE via ../aggregationOwnershipTestMet, which is the conservative direction here and is argued there.

Fact.Name: The trades or businesses in this aggregation meet at least two of the three stated factors
Fact.Description:
Requirement 3 of the Form 8995-A aggregation election, answered per aggregation row: "The trades or businesses meet at least two of the following factors" - (a) they provide products, property or services that are the same or that are customarily offered together; (b) they share facilities or share significant centralized business elements such as personnel, accounting, legal, manufacturing, purchasing, human resources or information technology resources; (c) they are operated in coordination with, or reliance upon, one or more of the businesses in the aggregated group (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 3, LEFT column).
ONE ANSWER, NOT THREE, and that is a deliberate narrowing rather than a shortcut. The printed rule's operative test is the two-of-three COUNT, and no line of Form 8995-A or its schedules asks which two. Three separate factor booleans plus a count would model the filer's reasoning rather than the form's question, and would let a return be refused for arithmetic this dictionary has no printed line to check. The filer applies the printed two-of-three test and answers the test's own outcome; the three factors are recited in this Description and in the authority comment so the answer is checkable against them.
IT IS READ ONLY ON AN AGGREGATION ROW, exactly as its ownership sibling above, and is complete-safe FALSE via ../aggregationFactorsTestMet.

Fact.Name: This trade or business is conducted with a specified agricultural or horticultural cooperative
Fact.Description:
Form 8995-A Part I line 1 column (e), "Check if patron". PER-BUSINESS, like every other line 1 column: a filer can market one trade's crop through a cooperative and run a second, unrelated trade that has no cooperative at all.
WHAT ANSWERING IT TRUE COSTS AND BUYS, both, which is the whole point of unit B. It turns on the line-14 patron reduction (UNFAVOURABLE, /qualifiedBusinesses/*/patronReduction) and it is also the gate on the line-38 section 199A(g) DPAD pass-through (FAVOURABLE, /qbi8995aDpadPassThrough, through /qbiHasPatronBusiness). Neither half of Schedule D (Form 8995-A) can be reached without the other: "Landing line 38 alone gives the patron the favourable half and none of the unfavourable half — an over-deduction."
Complete-safe FALSE when unanswered, via /qualifiedBusinesses/*/isPatron. That direction is the taxpayer-favourable one for line 14 taken alone, which is why the two allocable amounts become REQUIRED answers as soon as this flag is true — see /qualifiedBusinesses/*/isComplete.

Fact.Name: QBI from this trade or business allocable to qualified payments from the cooperative
Fact.Description:
Schedule D (Form 8995-A) line 2. The instruction is the definition: "Line 2. Input the QBI for the trade or business as properly allocable to qualified payments received from the cooperative. Qualified payments include patronage dividends and per-unit retains allocations" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 6). The statute says the same thing in the 9% leg — "so much of the qualified business income with respect to such trade or business as is properly allocable to qualified payments received from such cooperative" (IRC 199A(b)(7)(A), 26 U.S.C. 199A, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section199A&num=0&edition=2024, right column).
A SUBSET OF THIS ITEM'S OWN QBI, and the graph does NOT enforce that. It cannot: the filer states both, and a Limit may only carry a constant in this engine, not a cross-field dependency. The disclosed consequence is written out at /qualifiedBusinesses/*/qbiComponent, which is where an over-stated allocable amount would show up.
Min $0, NOT signed, and this is the same reasoning /writableQualifiedReitPtpLossCarryforwardFromPriorTaxYear records for its own limit. Schedule D's line 6 is a LESSER-OF that gets SUBTRACTED at Form 8995-A line 14, so a negative entry here would make the subtrahend negative and RAISE the deduction — a taxpayer-favourable answer to a line that exists only to lower it. The floor is what makes that unenterable. A genuinely negative QBI allocable to qualified payments is not a case Schedule D prints: line 2 has no parenthesised field.

Fact.Name: W-2 wages from this trade or business allocable to the qualified payments
Fact.Description:
Schedule D (Form 8995-A) line 4: "Enter the portion of W-2 wages from Form 8995-A, line 4, that are allocable to the qualified payments" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 6). The statute's 50% leg names the same quantity — "so much of the W-2 wages with respect to such trade or business as are properly allocable to such qualified payments" (IRC 199A(b)(7)(B), 26 U.S.C. 199A, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section199A&num=0&edition=2024, right column).
A PORTION OF ../writableW2Wages by the instruction's own words, and unenforced for the same reason its QBI twin is: the engine's Limit takes a constant, not a dependency. Min $0 for the same reason too — this feeds a subtrahend, so a negative entry would raise the deduction.
NOTE THE SOURCE LINE IT IS A PORTION OF: Form 8995-A line 4, the RAW allocable share of W-2 wages (../writableW2Wages), not the SSTB-reduced ../effectiveW2Wages. Schedule D prints no applicable-percentage step of its own.

Fact.Name: This business's Schedule C link resolves to an answered Schedule C
Fact.Description:
Whether ../linkedScheduleC actually reaches a Schedule C whose line 31 this graph can read. THE GUARD THE WHOLE UNIT TURNS ON, and its three terms are three separate ways the link can be present-looking and still supply nothing.
(1) THE LINK IS ANSWERED. An unanswered CollectionItem dereferences to nothing, so this term alone would nearly do — but it is written first because it is the one a reader expects and the other two are the ones a reader misses.
(2) THE RETURN CLAIMS SCHEDULE C INCOME. This term is not belt-and-braces; without it the guard is defeated outright. scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/tentativeProfit is a Switch on /claimsScheduleCIncome whose FALSE arm is a Complete $0, so on a return that carries /scheduleCs items while /hasScheduleCIncome is unanswered or false, the linked item's line 31 is a perfectly Complete $0 and term (3) passes. A business linked to such an item would then derive $0 and FILE CLEAN WHILE WHOLLY UNANSWERED — measurement (a) of the /qualifiedBusinesses/*/effectiveQbi contract, reproduced one level over.
(3) THE LINKED SCHEDULE C'S OWN LINE 31 IS COMPLETE. This is what distinguishes an UNANSWERED business from a $0 business, which is the whole of ground (a). With /claimsScheduleCIncome true, scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/tentativeProfit subtracts ../writableTotalExpenses from ../scheduleCGrossIncome through BARE dependencies with no complete-safe wrapper, so a /scheduleCs item nobody has answered has an INCOMPLETE line 31 and this term is false. THE MINUEND IS ../scheduleCGrossIncome, not ../writableGrossReceipts (Schedule C lines 2-7 are built). An item whose receipts and expenses ARE answered has a Complete line 31 — $0 included — and the derivation is allowed to be $0, because a business that earned nothing is a fact about the business rather than a fact about the interview.
TYPE: Boolean, ALWAYS Complete. That is load-bearing rather than tidy — this fact is read in a Switch When by ../usesScheduleCDerivedQbi, and Expression.switch's resultRecurse clears its accComplete flag on a When with no value, so an Incomplete here would turn ../qualifiedBusinessIncome Placeholder on every return that answers the collection. All three terms are IsComplete tests or a complete-safe gate, so none of them can be Incomplete.

Fact.Name: This Schedule C business's share of the self-employed health insurance deduction
Fact.Description: Schedule 1 line 17's self-employed health insurance deduction for the linked Schedule C business only. If exactly one business is attested as the plan business, this is the full Form 7206 line 14 amount only on that business's link. If no business is attested, the existing single-profitable-business fallback attributes it only to the linked Schedule C that has positive net profit, when there is no positive partnership K-1 term. Complete-safe $0 for a business that does not carry the plan. This is the Form 8995-A per-business twin of /qbiScheduleCSelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction.

Fact.Name: This Schedule C business's share of the self-employed retirement plan deduction
Fact.Description: The part of the Schedule 1 line 16 deduction for self-employed SEP, SIMPLE and qualified plans that is attributable to the linked Schedule C business: line 16 multiplied by that business's own net profit and divided by the total net profit of every profitable self-employment trade or business on the return (Form 7206 line 5). $0 for a linked business with no net profit. This is the Form 8995-A per-business twin of /qbiScheduleCSelfEmployedRetirementPlanDeduction: over the linked Schedule C businesses the shares add up to that return-level amount, so the deduction does not jump at the section 199A threshold.

Fact.Name: This Schedule C business's net profit when it is a profit
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 31 for this business when it is more than zero; $0 for a loss, a zero line 31 or an unanswered one. The numerator and the terms of the denominator for sharing the section 224 qualified tips exclusion among the Schedule C businesses.

Fact.Name: Total net profit of the profitable Schedule C businesses
Fact.Description: The sum of Schedule C line 31 over the Schedule C businesses that show a profit, losses left out. The denominator for sharing the section 224 qualified tips exclusion among them. Complete-safe: $0 when no Schedule C is entered.

Fact.Name: This Schedule C business's share of the section 224 qualified tips exclusion
Fact.Description: The part of the section 224 qualified tips deduction taken for tips received in a trade or business (/qbiScheduleCTipsExclusion) that this linked Schedule C business carries: that amount multiplied by this business's net profit and divided by the total net profit of the profitable Schedule C businesses. With one profitable Schedule C it is the whole amount; a linked business with no net profit carries $0. Over the linked businesses the shares add up to the return-level exclusion, so the exclusion leaves QBI once, not once per business, and the deduction does not jump at the section 199A threshold.

Fact.Name: This business's QBI derived from its own Schedule C (the per-business auto-derived amount)
Fact.Description:
The auto-derivation, attributed to a BUSINESS rather than to the return: this business's own Schedule C line 31, less the deductible half of self-employment tax, the self-employed health insurance deduction and the self-employed retirement plan deduction attributable to that same business, less its share of the section 224 qualified-tips exclusion, floored at $0. $0 whenever ../scheduleCLinkResolves is false, so an un-established link supplies nothing rather than a plausible zero.
IT IS /qbiAutoDerivedAmount ONE GRAIN DOWN. That fact is GreaterOf(scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax less /qbiScheduleCAttributableHalfSeTax less /qbiScheduleCSelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction less /qbiScheduleCSelfEmployedRetirementPlanDeduction less /qbiScheduleCTipsExclusion, $0) over the whole return; this one takes the same QBI items per business, with the health-insurance term taken only on the business identified by /scheduleCAttributableHealthInsuranceDeduction and the retirement plan term as each business's share in /scheduleCAttributableRetirementPlanDeduction. On the shape every committed return has — one Schedule C, no oil and gas working interest — the two are equal, because scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax is then that item's own nonexcluded line 31 and /qbiScheduleCAttributableHalfSeTax is that item's own share. SECTION 931/933: the minuend became this item's scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/netProfitSubjectToUsTax in the SAME COMMIT that moved /qbiAutoDerivedAmount's. This is the ABOVE-threshold (Form 8995-A) derivation and that is the BELOW-threshold (Form 8995) one; a section 933 filer whose income crossed the section 199A threshold would otherwise see the deduction JUMP for a reason no printed form describes — the defect shape a one-sided fix produces. Value-identical on every return that excludes nothing.
THE TIPS TERM IS THIS BUSINESS'S SHARE. /qbiScheduleCTipsExclusion is figured for the whole return, and no printed line splits qualified tips among businesses, so each linked business takes ../scheduleCAttributableTipsExclusion, the return amount in proportion to its net profit among the profitable Schedule C businesses (Treas. Reg. 1.199A-3(b)(5), a reasonable method). The shares add up to the return amount, so the exclusion leaves QBI once. At one profitable business it is the whole amount.
