THE FLOOR IS THE SAME ONE /qbiAutoDerivedAmount CARRIES and it means the same thing: a loss-making Schedule C derives $0 QBI here rather than a negative amount. A filer whose business ran a loss and who wants that loss on Form 8995 line 1 column (c) answers the amount, which still wins over this derivation.
ONE POPULATION THIS FILL MAKES REACHABLE AND DOES NOT SERVE, disclosed rather than left to be found: a return whose Schedule Cs net to a LOSS while at least one of them is profitable, with every QBI amount unanswered. Two businesses at +30,000 and (40,000), each linked, derive 30,000 and $0 here and /qbiSimplifiedAmount reports 30,000 — but /hasQualifiedTradeOrBusiness stays FALSE, because its Schedule C arm reads the RETURN-level scheduleC:/hasScheduleCNetProfit (positive-only, and this return's combined line 31 is negative) and its collection arm counts ANSWERED amounts, which a derived one is not. The deduction is therefore $0. Direction: UNDER-claiming, and visible — /qbiSimplifiedAmount shows the 30,000 the filer does not get. It is left alone deliberately: widening that gate to count derived businesses is a SECOND value-moving surface, taxpayer-favourable, and owes its own witness rather than riding this unit. A filer in this shape gets the deduction by answering the amount, which is the same door every other unserved QBI population uses.
SIGN/TYPE: Dollar, never negative, always Complete.
On a separate return that allocates community income, the minuend is the business's net profit less its Form 8958 line 5 column C, the per-business twin of /qbiAutoDerivedAmount's addend, so the deduction does not jump at the threshold.

Fact.Name: This business takes its QBI from its linked Schedule C rather than from an answer
Fact.Description:
Whether the per-business derivation supplies this business's QBI: the amount is UNANSWERED and ../scheduleCLinkResolves. THE ANSWER ALWAYS WINS — a filer who enters a business and answers its QBI, including an answered $0, has made a determination the derivation does not overrule, which is the same precedence /qbiSimplifiedAmount's Description records for the return-level fallback ("expressed by the PRESENCE OF AN ITEM rather than by an answered-zero scalar").
ANSWEREDNESS IS TESTED ON THE RAW WRITABLE for the reason /hasQualifiedTradeOrBusiness already gives: the complete-safe alias ../qualifiedBusinessIncome is always Complete and cannot tell an answered $0 from an unanswered field.
TYPE: Boolean, always Complete — see ../scheduleCLinkResolves for why that is load-bearing.

Fact.Name: This business's QBI is either answered or derivable from its Schedule C
Fact.Description:
The submission-gate term ../isComplete reads in place of the bare IsComplete(../writableQualifiedBusinessIncome): the QBI amount is answered, OR the per-business derivation supplies it.
THIS IS THE GATE RELAXATION, and it is the half of this unit that loosens rather than computes. It is safe only because ../usesScheduleCDerivedQbi is conditioned on the link actually RESOLVING — the /qualifiedBusinesses/*/effectiveQbi contract's measurement (a) named a relaxation "when the fallback supplies it" as a compute-wrong precisely because the return-level /qbiAutoDerivedAmount is $0 and Complete on a return with no Schedule C at all, so "the fallback supplies it" was true of every return and would have let a wholly unanswered business file clean at $0.
TYPE: Boolean, always Complete.

Fact.Name: Qualified business income (complete-safe, with the per-business derivation)
Fact.Description:
Complete-safe view of ../writableQualifiedBusinessIncome: the answer when it is answered, the per-business Schedule C derivation when it is not and ../linkedScheduleC resolves, $0 otherwise. MAY BE NEGATIVE when answered — the sign passes through unchanged; the derivation arm is floored at $0 by ../scheduleCDerivedQbi.
THE FALLBACK ARM IS deliberately HERE rather than on ../effectiveQbi. BOTH QBI paths read this alias — Form 8995 line 2 through /qbiSimplifiedAmount's CollectionSum, and the Form 8995-A ladder through ../effectiveQbi — so putting the fallback here moves them TOGETHER and the deduction cannot jump at the section 199A threshold. A fallback written onto ../effectiveQbi alone would have given the same filer $0 below the threshold and a derived amount above it: a new discontinuity running in the taxpayer-FAVOURABLE direction, which is the one that files clean and therefore the one the scope mandate treats as worse.
WHAT IT COSTS ON THE CORPUS: nothing. ../linkedScheduleC is new in this unit, so no committed scenario or node-test fixture answers it, ../usesScheduleCDerivedQbi is false everywhere, and this fact resolves exactly what it resolved before on all 86 committed files that answer /qualifiedBusinesses. Measured, not assumed — of those 86, ZERO also answer scheduleC:/scheduleCs, so every witness for the new arm is a fixture this unit builds.
THE ORDER OF THE THREE CASES IS THE PRECEDENCE and reads top to bottom: an answered amount (including an answered $0), then the derivation, then $0. See ../usesScheduleCDerivedQbi for why the answer wins.

Fact.Name: Allocable W-2 wages (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: Complete-safe view of ../writableW2Wages: $0 when unanswered.

Fact.Name: Allocable UBIA of qualified property (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: Complete-safe view of ../writableUbia: $0 when unanswered.

Fact.Name: This business is an SSTB (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: Complete-safe view of ../writableIsSstb: false when unanswered. The per-item successor of the retired return-level /qbiIsSstb.

Fact.Name: This line 1 row is an aggregation (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
Complete-safe view of ../writableIsAggregation: false when unanswered, which is also the printed default — a filer who never completes Schedule B is not aggregating.
THE Export IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS NOT A LINT WORKAROUND. No fact in this dictionary computes an AMOUNT from this flag, and none should: an aggregation is one Form 8995-A Part I column whose entered QBI, W-2 wages and UBIA are already combined across its members, so lines 2 through 16 are identical whether the row is one trade or business or twenty. The flag is a client-visible property of the row, so it is EXPORTED as well as consumed — the alternative readings (invent an arithmetic consumer, or skip-list it) would either fabricate arithmetic the form does not print or hide a fact from the wiring lint. Consuming ../writableIsAggregation keeps the writable grounded through this fact.
IT GAINED A CONSUMER AND THE SENTENCE ABOVE IS NARROWED, NOT DELETED. Until that day nothing at all read this flag, which is precisely what made the aggregation ELECTION free to claim: the printed election is conditional ("you may choose to aggregate multiple trades or businesses into a single trade or business for purposes of applying the limitations if you meet the following requirements", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 3, LEFT column) and the graph tested none of the conditions. ../hasIneligibleAggregation is now that test, and it is a REFUSAL rather than a computation — no amount moves because of this flag, which is why the paragraph above still stands with "amount" made explicit.

Fact.Name: This aggregation's common-ownership requirement is established (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
Complete-safe view of ../writableAggregationOwnershipTestMet: FALSE when unanswered, which here means NOT ESTABLISHED rather than DISPROVED.
THE DIRECTION IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE REST OF THIS COLLECTION AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT. Everywhere else in this module a complete-safe FALSE or $0 means the graph declines to claim something and the return under-states (../isSstb, ../isPatron, the two Schedule D amounts being the exception the submission door catches). Here FALSE is what makes ../hasIneligibleAggregation TRUE, so the unanswered state REFUSES the return. That is deliberate: aggregation exists to relax the per-column limitation ("You must combine the QBI, W-2 wages, and UBIA of qualified property for all aggregated trades or businesses, for purposes of applying the W-2 wage and UBIA of qualified property limitations", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 3), so an unanswered attestation defaulting to "eligible" would preserve exactly the silent taxpayer-FAVOURABLE over-deduction this pair was authored to close, while defaulting to "not established" costs an aggregating filer one answer and costs a non-aggregating filer nothing at all.
NOBODY IS REFUSED WHO WAS NOT ASKED. ../hasIneligibleAggregation reads this fact only inside its ../isAggregation arm, and ../isAggregation is itself complete-safe false, so the entire population this default can refuse is filers who affirmatively checked Form 8995-A Part I line 1(c). Measured at the fill (grep over scenarios/, zero hits): no committed scenario answered ../writableIsAggregation, so the refusal's live population was the node tests alone. That changed the same day — scenarios/units/qf3/qf3-unattested-aggregation-refused.json checks line 1(c) with neither attestation answered and is refused, beside its unaggregated twin qf3-same-economics-two-columns-clean.json which is not.

Fact.Name: This aggregation's two-of-three factors requirement is established (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: Complete-safe view of ../writableAggregationFactorsTestMet: FALSE when unanswered, meaning NOT ESTABLISHED. Same direction, same population and same argument as ../aggregationOwnershipTestMet above; the two are read as a conjunction by ../hasIneligibleAggregation, so either one unanswered or answered false refuses the aggregation on its own.

Fact.Name: This business is conducted with a specified cooperative (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
Complete-safe view of ../writableIsPatron: false when unanswered.
DIRECTION, stated because a complete-safe false is never neutral here: false means NO line-14 patron reduction, which OVER-states the deduction for a filer who is a patron and did not say so, and it also means NO line-38 DPAD, which UNDER-states it for the same filer. Both errors require the same unanswered checkbox and both are visible to the filer as a missing Schedule D. The alternative — refusing every return that leaves the box unanswered — would refuse the whole corpus, since a non-patron has nothing to check.

Fact.Name: Schedule D (Form 8995-A) line 2 (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
Complete-safe view of ../writableQbiAllocableToQualifiedPayments: $0 when unanswered. NON-NEGATIVE when answered (the writable carries Min $0).
THE $0 IS NOT A NEUTRAL DEFAULT AND IS NOT LEFT AS THE ANSWER. It drives the line-14 patron reduction to $0, which OVER-states the deduction — so a business whose ../isPatron is true and whose Schedule D amounts are unanswered is refused at submission by /qualifiedBusinesses/*/isComplete rather than filed with the reduction silently missing. The $0 exists so that the line-16 CollectionSum stays Complete, which is the same under-claim-in-the-graph, refuse-at-the-door split the rest of this collection uses; here the graph's error runs the other way (over-claim), which is exactly why the door clause is not optional.

Fact.Name: Schedule D (Form 8995-A) line 4 (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: Complete-safe view of ../writableW2WagesAllocableToQualifiedPayments: $0 when unanswered. NON-NEGATIVE when answered (the writable carries Min $0). Same direction note as its QBI twin above: an unanswered amount zeroes the patron reduction, which OVER-states the deduction, and the submission gate at /qualifiedBusinesses/*/isComplete is what stops that being filed.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 2 — this business's QBI after the SSTB applicable-percentage reduction
Fact.Description:
QBI entering Form 8995-A Part II line 2 for THIS trade, business, or aggregation. For a non-SSTB, the full per-item QBI. For an SSTB, QBI times the applicable percentage (Schedule A line 11) = QBI times (upper threshold minus taxable income before QBI, floored at 0) divided by the phase-in range width: zero above the upper threshold, ratably reduced within the phase-in range. Resolves only when Form 8995-A is claimed, so below-threshold and non-8995-A returns are unaffected — the same gate the retired return-level /qbiEffectiveQbi carried, kept deliberately so this migration moves no value.
MIGRATED, NOT REDESIGNED. The one behavioural change is that ../isSstb is per-business, which is the point: a filer with an SSTB and a non-SSTB business no longer gets the haircut applied to both or to neither.
THE ASYMMETRY IS CLOSED, AND THIS FACT'S BODY DID NOT MOVE. The paragraph this replaces said this fact "reads the per-item QBI, which does not see the Schedule C auto-derivation that /qbiSimplifiedAmount honours below the threshold", and named that as a deferred contract. The fix landed where the deferral said it belonged: on the SHARED alias ../qualifiedBusinessIncome, which now falls back to a per-business derivation off the business's own linked Schedule C. This fact reads that alias, so the Form 8995-A ladder sees the derivation without a character of this Derived changing — which is exactly why the contract for it insisted its successor "is NOT a rebody of this fact".
AND THE FIX IS NOT A REBODY OF THIS FACT, kept here because a reader of THIS Description would otherwise reach for the obvious change. Adding a per-item fallback to /qbiAutoDerivedAmount here would make the above-threshold path MORE generous than the below-threshold one for the same filer, not less: below the threshold an entered item whose QBI is unanswered contributes $0 to /qbiSimplifiedAmount's CollectionSum (the collection is answered and non-empty, so the auto-derivation arm is not reached), so a per-item fallback here would invent a NEW discontinuity running in the taxpayer-FAVOURABLE direction. The safe shape puts the fallback on the SHARED alias ../qualifiedBusinessIncome, which both paths read — that change moved only returns that could not be filed, because ../isComplete required IsComplete(../writableQualifiedBusinessIncome) on all four of its arms and /qbiHasIncompleteQualifiedBusinesses blocks submission on it. THAT LAST CLAUSE IS WHY THE FIX HAD TO BE A COUPLED PAIR, and it landed as one: the alias fallback plus the relaxation of that submission gate, in the same unit, so the population it serves is actually filable rather than merely differently-resolved. The gate's QBI term is now ../hasQbiAnswer.
THE THRESHOLD GATE ON THE HAIRCUT IS A DEFECT FIX, not a migration artefact. The applicable-percentage expression below is (upper threshold minus taxable income before QBI, floored at $0) over the phase-in range width. Above the threshold that is the correct §199A(d)(3)(B) percentage, running from 1 down to 0 across the band. BELOW the threshold it EXCEEDS 1 and the "reduction" INFLATES QBI: at 50,000 of taxable income it is (247,300 - 50,000) / 50,000 = 3.946, so an SSTB's 30,000 of QBI entered line 2 as 118,380. That is flatly contrary to the instructions — "Exception 1: If your 2025 taxable income before the QBI deduction isn't more than $394,600 if married filing jointly, and $197,300 for all other returns, your SSTB is treated as a qualified trade or business, and thus may generate income eligible for the QBI deduction" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 2), restated in the same instructions' overview as "At or below the threshold, you don't need to reduce your QBI" (line 58). The error was LATENT while nothing below the threshold reached Form 8995-A, and the routing fix in this same unit would have made it LIVE and taxpayer-FAVOURABLE — a silent over-deduction that files clean, which is the worse of the two directions. The gate is /isAboveQbiThreshold, whose strict greater-than matches the instruction's inclusive "isn't more than". Its siblings ../effectiveW2Wages and ../effectiveUbia carry the identical fix for the identical reason.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 4 — this business's W-2 wages after the SSTB applicable-percentage reduction
Fact.Description:
W-2 wages entering Form 8995-A line 4 for THIS trade, business, or aggregation. Full wages for a non-SSTB; for an SSTB, wages times the applicable percentage (Schedule A line 12) = wages times (upper threshold minus TI, floored at 0) divided by the phase-in range width, ABOVE THE THRESHOLD ONLY. The per-item successor of the retired return-level /qbiEffectiveW2Wages, body otherwise unchanged.
THE THRESHOLD GATE has the identical fix as ../effectiveQbi, where the full reasoning and the authorities are recorded. Short form: below the threshold the ratio exceeds 1, so the "reduction" inflated wages; the instructions' Exception 1 treats a below-threshold SSTB as a fully qualified trade or business. Nothing below the threshold READS this fact once the line 3 skip lands at ../qbiComponent (lines 4 through 12 are skipped), so the gate is belt-and-braces here rather than load-bearing — but leaving one sibling of three ungated would be an invitation to a later reader.
A THIRD ARM, AND IT IS FIRST. The printed Note "If the adjusted QBI from the trade or business is zero or less after the reduction for loss netting, then the amount reported for W-2 wages and UBIA of qualified property must be zero for that trade or business, as the W-2 wages and UBIA of qualified property from that trade or business aren't allowed in computing your QBI limitations" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 6) had no arm here at all: only the SSTB case and the /claims8995A case existed, so a column whose ../adjustedQbi went zero or negative through loss netting still reported its full W-2 wages on line 4 and its full UBIA on line 7. The finding recorded the direction as print-only, and it still is - the four Export mirrors that read the limit legs move no deduction - but the row asked for the fix before a fifth consumer made it live. The same arm is on ../effectiveUbia, which the Note names in the same sentence.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 7 — this business's UBIA after the SSTB applicable-percentage reduction
Fact.Description:
UBIA entering Form 8995-A line 7 for THIS trade, business, or aggregation. Full UBIA for a non-SSTB; for an SSTB, UBIA times the applicable percentage (Schedule A line 13) = UBIA times (upper threshold minus TI, floored at 0) divided by the phase-in range width, ABOVE THE THRESHOLD ONLY. The per-item successor of the retired return-level /qbiEffectiveUbia, body otherwise unchanged.
THE THRESHOLD GATE is the third of the identical triple; see ../effectiveQbi for the reasoning and the authorities, and ../effectiveW2Wages for why it is belt-and-braces on this fact rather than load-bearing.

Fact.Name: Schedule C (Form 8995-A) — this business's QBI when it is QBI and not a loss
Fact.Description:
This trade or business's Form 8995-A line 2 amount when that amount is positive, and $0 when it is a loss. The Schedule C apportionment rule names exactly this population twice: the loss "must be apportioned among all your trades or businesses with QBI in proportion to their QBI" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 6), spelled out again at the column itself as "Apportion the amount from line 5 among all your trades or businesses with QBI, but not loss, in proportion to their QBI" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 6).
WHY THIS IS A FACT RATHER THAN AN INLINE GreaterOf: it is summed. /qbiTotalPositiveQbi is a CollectionSum over this path and is the apportionment DENOMINATOR, and the same per-item value is the NUMERATOR at ../lossNettingAdjustment. A collection sum needs a per-item fact to sum.
IT READS ../effectiveQbi, NOT THE RAW WRITABLE, and the order is the instructions' own: the Part I question list puts the SSTB question ("Do you have an SSTB? If yes, see Schedule A") before the loss question ("Did any of your trades, businesses, or aggregations have QBI for the year ... If yes, complete Schedule C") — both in the Part I question list at https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 6 — so Schedule A has already run and the amount Schedule C nets is the post-applicable-percentage one.
COMPLETENESS: inherits ../effectiveQbi's, which resolves only when Form 8995-A is claimed. Off that path this fact is Incomplete and absent, exactly like the rest of the line 2-13 ladder.

Fact.Name: Schedule C (Form 8995-A) — total QBI of the businesses with QBI but not loss
Fact.Description:
The apportionment DENOMINATOR: the sum of /qualifiedBusinesses/*/positiveQbi over every entered trade or business. "Apportion the amount from line 5 among all your trades or businesses with QBI, but not loss, in proportion to their QBI" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 6) — a share "in proportion to their QBI" is this business's QBI over the total QBI of that same population, and this is the total.
THE /claims8995A + IsComplete GATE IS THE /qbi8995aQbiComponent SHAPE, restated for the same two measured reasons that fact's own Description records. A bare CollectionSum would resolve Complete $0 on every return in the corpus, adding a row to all 938 committed cases where the rest of this ladder is Incomplete and absent; and an ABSENT collection is not an answered-empty one, so the IsComplete wrapper is what keeps the ~250 cases that never answer /qualifiedBusinesses from flipping Complete to Placeholder.
ZERO IS A LEGITIMATE VALUE HERE, and it is why ../lossNettingAdjustment tests it before dividing: a return whose every column is a loss has no business "with QBI" to apportion against, so the denominator is $0 and no apportionment happens at all. That case is not an error and is not a division by zero — it is a return whose whole current-year loss becomes the section 199A(c)(2) carryforward, which SHIPS at /qualifiedBusinessNetLossCarryforwardToNextYear (the clause this replaces read "this unit does not build").

Fact.Name: Schedule C (Form 8995-A) — current-year QBI of every business, netted
Fact.Description:
The sum of /qualifiedBusinesses/*/effectiveQbi over every entered trade or business, losses signed negative. This is what "Schedule C (Form 8995-A) offsets your trade or business that generated a qualified business loss against the QBI from your other trades or businesses" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 6) produces: one netted current-year figure across the columns.
ITS ONLY CONSUMER IS /qbiAggregateQualifiedBusinessLoss, which subtracts the positive total from it to isolate the loss. Stated as its own fact rather than inlined because it is also the quantity the section 199A(c)(2) carryforward reads. Naming it as its own fact is what kept that unit from having to re-cut this one.
THE CARRY-IN IS AT SCHEDULE C LINE 2, AND THIS FACT IS ITS ABOVE-THRESHOLD HALF. /qualifiedBusinessNetLossCarryforwardIn is SUBTRACTED here because it stores a positive MAGNITUDE, so a prior-year qualified business net loss joins the SAME pool Schedule C apportions across the profitable columns rather than being applied beside it. That placement is the schedule's own, on two printed statements rather than on preference. (1) Schedule C is mandatory when EITHER a current-year loss exists OR a carryforward does: "If any of your trades, businesses, or aggregations have a qualified business loss for the current year or you have a qualified business net loss carryforward from prior years, you must complete Schedule C (Form 8995-A) before starting Form 8995-A, Part I" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 6). (2) Its computation order puts lines 2 through 5 INSIDE the amount line 1 column (b) apportions: "Note: The line items for this schedule are computed out of order: first figure line 1, column (a); then skip to lines 2 through 5; and come back to line 1, columns (b) and (c)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 6). With ONE profitable column and no current-year loss the apportionment is the identity, so the carryforward lands on that column intact; with several it is split in proportion to their QBI, which is what the schedule says to do with a qualified business loss however it arose.
BYTE-IDENTICAL ON EVERY COMMITTED RETURN: no scenario and no node-test fixture answers /writableQualifiedBusinessNetLossCarryforwardFromPriorTaxYear, its alias is complete-safe $0, and subtracting $0 leaves this fact's resolved value exactly where it was.
THE OTHER LEG LANDED THE SAME DAY, Schedule C line 6 — this fact floored at $0 from above, carried OUT to next year, at /qualifiedBusinessNetLossCarryforwardToNextYear. Its contract was grown by the carry-IN fill under the same carry-IN-then-carry-OUT precedent /qualifiedReitPtpLossCarryforwardToNextYear set, and the carry-OUT fill closed it. The paragraph this replaces said that until it landed, a return whose every column is a loss drops the carryforward entirely — /qbiTotalPositiveQbi is $0, the apportionment guard is false, and nothing carries the residual. The first three clauses are still true and the last one is not: this fact is exactly what the carry-OUT reads on that return, so the residual now leaves by line 6 instead of vanishing.
SIGN: MAY BE NEGATIVE, and no floor is written here. The floor the printed forms carry is downstream and per-column (Form 8995-A line 13's greater-of against a $0 line 12, Form 8995 line 4's "If zero or less, enter -0-"); a floor at this node would silently discard the very loss the carryforward successor has to see.

Fact.Name: Schedule C (Form 8995-A) — the aggregate qualified business loss to apportion
Fact.Description:
The amount Schedule C line 1, column (b) apportions ("the amount from line 5"), expressed as the netted current-year total less the positive-only total. Identically: the sum of the negative columns. NEGATIVE OR ZERO by construction, since /qbiTotalNetQbi is /qbiTotalPositiveQbi plus the loss columns.
WHY THE SUBTRACTION RATHER THAN A SECOND per-item MIN AND SUM: the two forms are arithmetically the same and this one costs one fact instead of two, but the real reason is that both of its operands are already load-bearing on their own — the positive total is the apportionment denominator and the netted total is what the carryforward successor reads. A third summed per-item view would be a quantity nothing else needs.
ZERO MEANS SCHEDULE C DOES NOTHING, which is the value-neutrality this unit's byte-identity claim rests on. Every return in the committed corpus carries at most ONE qualified business, so either that business has QBI (this fact is $0) or it has a loss (the DENOMINATOR is $0); ../lossNettingAdjustment requires BOTH a positive denominator and a strictly negative aggregate loss before it moves anything, so on every one of those returns it is $0 and ../adjustedQbi is ../effectiveQbi unchanged.

Fact.Name: Schedule C (Form 8995-A) line 1, column (b) — this business's loss-netting adjustment
Fact.Description:
Schedule C (Form 8995-A) line 1, column (b), for THIS trade or business: "Apportion the amount from line 5 among all your trades or businesses with QBI, but not loss, in proportion to their QBI" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 6).
THREE ARMS, and which one applies is decided by the two return-level totals, not by this item alone: * NO NETTING TO DO — $0. Either there is no business with QBI to apportion against (/qbiTotalPositiveQbi is $0) or there is no loss to apportion (/qbiAggregateQualifiedBusinessLoss is not negative). Both tests are required: a single-business return satisfies one or the other whichever way its QBI runs, which is why this unit moves no committed value. * A BUSINESS WITH QBI — its proportional share of the loss, negative: the aggregate loss times (this business's QBI over the total QBI of the businesses with QBI). * A BUSINESS WITH A LOSS — the negation of its own line 2, so that column (c) below comes out at $0. The loss has been moved into the other columns' adjustments and counting it a second time in its own column is precisely the double-count Schedule C exists to prevent. The printed schedule computes its columns "out of order" for the same reason (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 6).
CONSERVATION IS THE PROPERTY THAT MAKES THIS A RE-ALLOCATION AND NOT A GIVE-AWAY: the adjusted amounts sum back to /qbiTotalNetQbi, because the profitable columns absorb exactly the aggregate loss and the loss columns are zeroed. Both multi-column node tests assert the sum as well as the parts, so the property is pinned rather than asserted.
THE ROUNDING RESIDUAL, disclosed rather than left for a reader to find. The share is a division in integer cents, so with N profitable columns the apportioned amounts can sum to the aggregate loss plus or minus up to N cents, and conservation is exact only up to that bound. The drift is bounded by cents, runs in either direction rather than one-sidedly in the taxpayer's favour, and the alternative — apportioning N-1 columns and giving the remainder to the last — would make the answer depend on collection ORDER, which is a worse property than a cent. The printed schedule gives no rounding rule to follow.
NOT AN ELECTION, AND NOT SCHEDULE B. This is mandatory netting between unaggregated trades or businesses; the Schedule B aggregation ELECTION is a different, optional schedule a filer with two unaggregated businesses never touches (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 6).

Fact.Name: Schedule C (Form 8995-A) line 1, column (c) — adjusted QBI, the amount Form 8995-A line 2 receives
Fact.Description:
Schedule C (Form 8995-A) line 1, column (c) for THIS trade or business: line 1 column (a) plus line 1 column (b), i.e. ../effectiveQbi plus ../lossNettingAdjustment. "Line 1, column (c). Enter this amount on the corresponding line on Form 8995-A, Part II" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 6) — so this, not ../effectiveQbi, is what Form 8995-A line 2 holds once a loss exists anywhere on the return, and ../twentyPctQbi (line 3) reads it.
WHY ../effectiveQbi WAS NOT SIMPLY REBODIED. It keeps its own name and its own contract: it is the post-Schedule-A amount, the thing Schedule C line 1 column (a) asks for, and the auto-derivation gap is about THAT quantity. Folding the netting into it would have hidden a schedule inside a fact named for a different one.
NO FLOOR AT $0, AND THE FORM SAYS SO OUT LOUD. When the aggregate loss exceeds the total QBI it is apportioned against, a profitable column's adjusted amount goes negative, and the instructions contemplate exactly that: "Note: If the adjusted QBI from the trade or business is zero or less after the reduction for loss netting, then the amount reported for W-2 wages and UBIA of qualified property must be zero for that trade or business" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 6). A floor here would also discard the residual the section 199A(c)(2) carryforward has to carry.
THAT NOTE IS NOT SEPARATELY IMPLEMENTED, AND HERE IS THE PROOF IT DOES NOT NEED TO BE — written out rather than left as a silent judgement, because "the instructions say to do X and we do not" is the kind of gap a reader must be able to check. The Note's only effect is to zero ../effectiveW2Wages and ../effectiveUbia for a column whose adjusted QBI is zero or less. Those two facts have exactly one consumer between them, ../wageUbiaLimit (line 10), and line 10 reaches the deduction through only two paths: * LINE 11 is the LESSER of line 3 and line 10. When this fact is zero or less, line 3 is zero or less and line 10 is never negative, so line 3 is the lesser whatever line 10 holds — zeroing line 10 cannot change line 11. * LINE 12 applies only when line 10 is LESS THAN line 3. With line 3 zero or less and line 10 never negative, that test is false whatever line 10 holds — zeroing line 10 cannot change line 12 either. So the Note is arithmetically inert on this graph, and implementing it would change the resolved values of three facts (../effectiveW2Wages, ../effectiveUbia, ../wageUbiaLimit) while changing no line of any return — a change the append-only delta store would have to absorb for no correctness gain. If a future unit gives ../effectiveW2Wages or ../effectiveUbia a SECOND consumer outside the line-10 chain, this proof lapses and the Note must then be built; that condition is the trigger, not a date.
BYTE-IDENTICAL ON EVERY COMMITTED RETURN. Each of the 54 committed scenarios and node-test fixtures that answer /qualifiedBusinesses carries at most one item, and with one item ../lossNettingAdjustment is $0 on both of its guards, so this fact equals ../effectiveQbi and ../twentyPctQbi is unmoved.

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 16 / Schedule C (Form 8995-A) line 6 — the qualified business net (loss) carryforward OUT to next year
Fact.Description:
Form 8995 line 16, "Total qualified business (loss) carryforward. Combine lines 2 and 3. If greater than zero, enter -0-" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8995.pdf, page 1, printed with a parenthesised entry field), and Schedule C (Form 8995-A) line 6, the same amount on the above-threshold form. Line 6's instruction is what makes the pair a loop: "The amount reported on this line must be reported in the next tax year on Schedule C (Form 8995-A), line 2, or Form 8995, line 3, Qualified business net (loss) carryforward from prior years, as applicable. This amount will offset QBI in subsequent tax years regardless of whether it is reported and whether the trade or business that generated the loss is still in existence" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 6). The carry-IN half of the pair is /writableQualifiedBusinessNetLossCarryforwardFromPriorTaxYear and its complete-safe alias, above.
IT IS NOT THE CARRY-IN NEGATED AND IT IS NOT THE NETTED TOTAL NEGATED EITHER. It is that total floored at $0 FROM ABOVE, so a return with more QBI than loss carries nothing forward at all and only the part the current year could not absorb survives. The printed ceiling on the signed amount ("If greater than zero, enter -0-") is a FLOOR once the amount is stored as a magnitude, which is what the GreaterOf below writes. NEVER BOTH, and the exact wording matters at the boundary: line 4 is positive exactly when line 16 is $0 and line 16 is positive exactly when line 4 is floored to $0, but at exact absorption BOTH are $0, so the claim is "at most one is nonzero" and not "exactly one" — the N/N+1 pair is what makes that distinction visible. At exact absorption line 4 is exactly $0 before the floor and this fact is $0, the case where neither carries; one dollar over, line 4 is -1.00 and this fact is 1.00.
ONE FACT WITH TWO ARMS, which is the question this node's contract refused to let the fill leave unasked. The selector is /qbiUsesForm8995A — the SAME fact taxCalculations /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction selects its own two arms on — so the carry-out is read off whichever form the filer actually works: Schedule C's netting (/qbiTotalNetQbi) on Form 8995-A, Form 8995 line 4 before its floor (/qbiSimplifiedAmount) on the simplified form. A selector that did not match the deduction's would let a return compute its deduction from one form and its carryforward from the other.
WHERE THE TWO ARMS ACTUALLY DIVERGE, worked out rather than assumed, because for most returns they are the same number and a reader should know which ones are not. /qualifiedBusinesses/*/effectiveQbi applies the SSTB applicable-percentage haircut only above the section 199A threshold (its Switch tests /isAboveQbiThreshold), so BELOW the threshold effectiveQbi is ../qualifiedBusinessIncome unchanged and the two sources reduce to the same CollectionSum less the same carry-IN — including on a multi-column all-loss return, since neither source floors. They part company in exactly two populations: * AN SSTB ABOVE THE THRESHOLD, where /qbiTotalNetQbi carries the Schedule A reduction into the pool and /qbiSimplifiedAmount does not. This arm is REASONED, NOT MEASURED, and deliberately so: whether Schedule A's applicable-percentage reduction flows into the section 199A(c)(2) carryover pool is not stated by any printed line this repo holds, so this fact takes /qbiTotalNetQbi's composition as its own contract named it rather than pinning a dollar onto an unsourced reading. The authority note carries the UNWITNESSED clause; a node test asserting a carry-out for that population would be a citation this repo cannot make. * A RETURN WITH NO ANSWERED /qualifiedBusinesses COLLECTION, where /qbiSimplifiedAmount falls back to the Schedule C auto-derivation and /qbiTotalNetQbi does not resolve at all. That is why the gate below carries IsComplete(/qualifiedBusinesses) as a second conjunct rather than /qbiUsesForm8995A alone: /qbiUsesForm8995A is All(/claims8995A, Any(threshold, patron)) and none of those three imply an answered collection, so the bare selector would make this fact INCOMPLETE for an opted-in filer with no per-business detail — a filer who has a carryforward and no way to see it. Mirroring the source fact's own gate sends that population to the simplified arm, which resolves for everyone.
SIGN — POSITIVE MAGNITUDE, AND THE ROUND-TRIP IS WHY, the same test /qualifiedReitPtpLossCarryforwardToNextYear set and passed. Whatever this stores must be answerable DIRECTLY into next year's /writableQualifiedBusinessNetLossCarryforwardFromPriorTaxYear, which carries Min $0 and would REFUSE a signed negative. Magnitude out, magnitude in, subtract at the consumer — one convention end to end across both halves of the pair.
WHAT IT CLOSES, and this is the reason it is a successor rather than a nicety. The carry-IN fill disclosed a residual: above the threshold the apportionment needs a business "with QBI, but not loss" to apportion against, so a return whose every column is a loss has a $0 denominator, /qualifiedBusinesses/*/lossNettingAdjustment stays $0 on its own guard, and the carry-IN moves nothing that year. THIS is where that loss goes. Three authority notes carried that shape as their UNWITNESSED clause (/qbiTotalNetQbi, /qbiTotalPositiveQbi and /qualifiedBusinesses/*/lossNettingAdjustment) and all three are corrected in this landing.
CONSUMER: none in this tax year, by construction. It carries <Export downstreamFacts="true"/> and deliberately NOT mef="true", exactly as /qualifiedReitPtpLossCarryforwardToNextYear does and for that fact's own restated reason: NOTHING in this module is mef-exported. The whole QBI chain reaches MeF through taxCalculations:/qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction alone, the only QBI row in dictionary/manifest/spine-registry.tsv, so tagging line 16 would make it the single transmitted line of a form whose every other line is untransmitted. TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, POSITIVE MAGNITUDE (never negative — the floor is the whole point), no rounding at this node.
Multi-year carryovers are blocked by design where state is READ FROM a prior year; a carryover item is a cross-year unit in which one unit authors the ending-balance fact in the earlier year's dictionary. This fact reads none: its inputs are this return's own current-year columns and the ATTESTED carry-IN the filer states. This is that ending-balance half. Multi-year PROJECTION stays excluded and the cross-year MECHANISM itself is still absent: the pair runs on the attested carry-IN in the interim, exactly as the REIT/PTP pair and Schedule D's two capital-loss carryovers do. NO CYCLE, RE-VERIFIED ON DISK RATHER THAN TAKEN FROM THE CONTRACT. This fact is a pure sink: nothing in this return reads it, which is why it is exported and wired to no consumer here. The edge that could look circular is the selector: /qbiUsesForm8995A reaches /isAboveQbiThreshold and thence /taxableIncomeBeforeQbi, which reads taxCalculations /agi — and the QBI deduction is itself a term of taxable income. That loop is already broken one fact upstream and not by this one: /taxableIncomeBeforeQbi exists precisely to be taxable income figured BEFORE the QBI deduction, "Used as the income base for the 20% cap to avoid a circular dependency" in its own words, and the whole deduction ladder already depends on it. This fact adds no edge that ladder does not already carry.
CORPUS IMPACT: purely ADDITIVE. No committed scenario answers the carry-IN writable and none has a negative netted total, so this fact resolves Complete $0 on every committed return and changes no existing row. Its nonzero behaviour is witnessed by node tests rather than by scenarios, which is the same position its REIT/PTP sibling occupies.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 3 — 20% of this business's QBI
Fact.Description:
20% of the per-item QBI. Form 8995-A line 3, a per-COLUMN line. The per-item successor of the retired return-level /qbi8995aTwentyPctQbi.
IT READS ../adjustedQbi AS OF THE SCHEDULE C UNIT, not ../effectiveQbi. Line 2 holds what Schedule C (Form 8995-A) line 1 column (c) puts there — "Enter this amount on the corresponding line on Form 8995-A, Part II" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 6) — and with no loss anywhere on the return the two are the same value, which is why every committed single-item case is unmoved. This one re-point is the whole wiring of the netting into the ladder: ../effectiveQbi has no other consumer, so there is no second path left reading the pre-netting amount.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 10 — this business's W-2 wage / UBIA limit
Fact.Description: The greater of (50% of W-2 wages) or (25% of W-2 wages + 2.5% of UBIA), for THIS trade, business, or aggregation. Form 8995-A line 10, a per-COLUMN line. The per-item successor of the retired return-level /qbi8995aWageUbiaLimit, body unchanged.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 11 — smaller of 20% QBI or this business's wage/UBIA limit
Fact.Description:
The wage/UBIA-limited amount for THIS trade, business, or aggregation: the smaller of Form 8995-A line 3 (20% of QBI) or line 10 (the wage/UBIA limit). Form 8995-A line 11, a per-COLUMN line. The per-item successor of the retired return-level /qbi8995aLimitation, body unchanged.
THIS FACT RESOLVES BELOW THE THRESHOLD AND IS NOT READ THERE. Line 3's own instruction sends a filer with taxable income of $197,300 or less ($394,600 MFJ) straight from line 3 to line 13, skipping lines 4 through 12 — so on that side of the threshold line 11 is a line the filer never fills in. The skip is implemented one level up, at ../qbiComponent, which selects line 3 directly rather than this fact; making THIS fact Incomplete below the threshold would have contaminated the GreaterOf it feeds instead. A reader who finds a live line-11 value on a below-threshold return has found dead weight, not a computation.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 12/26 — this business's QBI after the phased-in reduction
Fact.Description: Applies only within the phase-in range when the wage/UBIA limit (line 10) is less than 20% of QBI (line 3): line 3 minus (line 3 minus line 10) times the phase-in percentage ((taxable income before QBI minus threshold) / phase-in range). Otherwise $0. Form 8995-A Part III line 26, carried to line 12 — both per-COLUMN lines (Part III carries the same A/B/C column headers as Part II). The per-item successor of the retired return-level /qbi8995aPhasedInReduction, body unchanged; the phase-in percentage's numerator and denominator stay return-level because they are functions of taxable income, not of the business.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 14 — this business's patron reduction (Schedule D line 6)
Fact.Description:
Form 8995-A line 14, "Patron reduction. Enter the amount from Schedule D (Form 8995-A), line 6, if any", which the Line 14 instruction spells out in full: "Patrons of agricultural or horticultural cooperatives are required to reduce their QBI component by the lesser of: 9% of QBI allocable to qualified payments from a specified cooperative, or 50% of W-2 wages allocable to qualified payments" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 7). The statute is the same lesser-of, per trade or business: IRC 199A(b)(7) reduces "the amount determined under paragraph (2) with respect to such trade or business ... by the lesser of — (A) 9 percent of so much of the qualified business income with respect to such trade or business as is properly allocable to qualified payments received from such cooperative, or (B) 50 percent of so much of the W-2 wages with respect to such trade or business as are properly allocable to such qualified payments" (26 U.S.C. 199A, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section199A&num=0&edition=2024 left column, continued at lines 90-103 right column).
SCHEDULE D'S LINES 1-6 COLLAPSE INTO THIS ONE FACT, deliberately, and the collapse is arithmetic rather than editorial: line 1 is the trade or business NAME (no consumer in this repo — the wiring lint blocks an unconsumed fact and inventing an Export for a display string is scope creep, invariant #7), line 3 is 9% of line 2 and line 5 is 50% of line 4, so lines 3 and 5 are single Multiply nodes with no independent meaning, and line 6 is the lesser of them. What DOES get its own fact is each of the two INPUTS, because each is a filer answer. Schedule D (Form 8995-A) itself is NOT vendored — sources/ holds Form 8995-A pages 1-2 and the instructions, and the instructions are what define lines 2, 4 and 6 — so the line numbering above is quoted from the instructions, not read off the schedule.
WHY THE per-BUSINESS GRAIN. Line 14 sits under Form 8995-A Part I's A/B/C column headers with lines 2 through 15, and the statute reduces "the amount determined under paragraph (2) with respect to such trade or business". A patron with two trades, only one of which is conducted with the cooperative, reduces only that one.
NOT A PATRON, $0, AND THE DIRECTION OF THAT $0: it OVER-states the deduction for a patron who left the line 1(e) checkbox unanswered, which UNDER-taxes that filer. The checkbox is the only thing that can turn it on, and answering it true immediately makes both Schedule D amounts REQUIRED at /qualifiedBusinesses/*/isComplete — so the over-statement survives only for a filer who never told the graph they were a patron at all.
WHAT THIS FACT DOES NOT MODEL, disclosed: Schedule D's line 2 asks for QBI "properly allocable to qualified payments", and the graph reads it as the filer states it, with no SSTB applicable-percentage haircut applied — Schedule D prints no such step, and its line 4 is explicitly a portion of Form 8995-A line 4, the RAW allocable wages. For an SSTB patron that leaves line 14 computed on unreduced amounts while line 13 is computed on reduced ones. The consequence is bounded and stated at ../qbiComponent.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 15 — this business's qualified business income component
Fact.Description:
Form 8995-A line 13, "Qualified business income deduction before patron reduction. Enter the greater of line 11 or line 12", then line 15, "Qualified business income component. Subtract line 14 from line 13". THE LINE 11 / LINE 12 GreaterOf MOVED DOWN HERE from the return-level /qbi8995aQbiComponent, where it never belonged: line 13 is a per-COLUMN line on the printed form and always was, and line 16 ("Add all amounts reported on line 15", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8995a.pdf, page 1) is the only line that legitimately spans columns.
LINE 14, THE PATRON REDUCTION, IS REAL AS OF UNIT B and this fact is a REBODY: the Subtract that unit A deliberately did not write — "line 14 (the patron reduction) is $0 until unit B, so no Subtract is written rather than a Subtract of a hardcoded zero" — is now written, over ../patronReduction. For every non-patron, and for every return in the corpus before this unit, ../patronReduction is $0 and this fact is byte-identical to unit A's GreaterOf.
NO FLOOR AT $0, AND THAT IS A DECISION, not an omission — the unit-B contract required this fill to "state whether it floors line 15 explicitly or relies on that". IT RELIES ON IT, and here is the proof it relies on. For internally consistent answers line 14 can never exceed line 13: line 14 = min(9% x allocable QBI, 50% x allocable wages) and, since the allocable amounts are portions of this business's own QBI and wages, that is at most min(9% x QBI, 50% x wages) which is at most min(20% x QBI, 50% x wages) = min(line 3, at most line 10), which is at most line 11, which is at most line 13. The printed form prints no floor on line 15 and no parenthesised entry field, so inventing one would be adding an unprinted rule.
THE RESIDUAL THE PROOF LEAVES, disclosed rather than absorbed. The chain above assumes the allocable amounts really are portions of this item's QBI and wages, and nothing enforces that: the engine's Limit takes a constant, not a cross-field dependency. Two ways to break it, both filer data errors rather than graph errors — answering allocable QBI larger than the business's own QBI, and an SSTB whose line 2 has been cut by the applicable percentage while the stated allocable amount has not. Either can drive line 15 negative, which would reduce the line-16 sum. A floor would MASK that error in the taxpayer's favour rather than surface it, so it is not written; what is written is this paragraph.
THE FLOOR IS NOW WRITTEN, and the paragraph above is kept as the record of why it was not. Two things it got wrong. First, "The printed form prints no floor on line 15" is true of the FORM and false of the INSTRUCTIONS, which are the authority the comment below already cites: "Line 15. Subtract the patron reduction on line 14 from the amount on line 13. If zero or less, enter zero." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 7). So the floor is printed, and writing it is not inventing an unprinted rule. Second, the proof that line 14 can never exceed line 13 holds only for the ABOVE-threshold regime it was written against. Below the threshold line 13 is line 3 outright, and line 3 is 20% of an ../adjustedQbi that Schedule C's loss netting can drive NEGATIVE, so line 15 = a negative line 13 minus a positive line 14, with no filer data error needed. A NEGATIVE deduction adds to taxable income; the taxpayer was OVER-charged by the tax on it. All three resolve 0.00 now. The masking concern the paragraph raises is answered where the printed form answers it: the unfloored magnitudes stay visible on ../adjustedQbi and ../twentyPctQbi, which this fix deliberately leaves alone.
WHAT THIS FIX DOES NOT DO, named rather than absorbed. Two further printed rules in the same finding are NOT written here, because both move values that committed fixtures pin and both deserve their own unit: (1) Schedule C (Form 8995-A) line 1 column (c) is headed "(Combine (a) and (b). If zero or less, enter -0-.)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8995ac.pdf, page 1) and ../adjustedQbi carries no such floor - flooring it moves the negatives the loss-netting columns now carry; (2) ../lossNettingAdjustment spreads the UNCAPPED /qbiAggregateQualifiedBusinessLoss where printed line 5 is "the smaller of the absolute value of line 3 or line 4" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8995ac.pdf, page 1), so column (b) can exceed what the form allocates. Neither changes the Form 1040 deduction once line 15 is floored.
COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION, through the per-item views its ladder reads: a business whose QBI, wages, UBIA, SSTB flag and Schedule D amounts are all unanswered contributes $0 to line 16 rather than making the whole sum Incomplete and blanking the deduction for the businesses that WERE answered. Filing such a return is refused separately at /qbiHasIncompleteQualifiedBusinesses.
LINE 13 HAS TWO REGIMES, and the second one is printed on line 3 rather than on line 13: "Multiply line 2 by 20% (0.20). If your taxable income is $197,300 or less ($394,600 if married filing jointly), skip lines 4 through 12 and enter the amount from line 3 on line 13" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8995a.pdf, page 1). So below the threshold line 13 is line 3 outright: the W-2 wage / UBIA limitation (line 11) and the phased-in reduction (line 12) are not computed at all. The shipping ladder applied line 11 with NO threshold gate. Unit B's own cap-boundary fixtures dodged it by choosing wages high enough that line 3 bound anyway, which a reader must not mistake for the graph implementing the skip.
THE SKIP ARM IS SCOPED TO FILERS ACTUALLY ON FORM 8995-A (/qbiUsesForm8995A), NOT TO EVERY BELOW-THRESHOLD RETURN, and that is a scope decision with a consequence worth naming. A Form 8995-A line-3 instruction governs a filer working Form 8995-A; a below-threshold non-patron belongs on Form 8995 by that form's own header (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8995.pdf, page 1) and the Form 8995-A "Who Can Take the Deduction" test does not admit them (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 1). THE RESIDUAL, disclosed rather than absorbed: a below-threshold non-patron who nonetheless answers /writableClaims8995A true still runs the unskipped ladder here, so this fact and /qbi8995aQbiComponent hold a WRONG line-13 amount for them — $0 rather than 20% of QBI when their answered W-2 wages are $0. NOTHING READS IT. Their Form 1040 line 13 comes from taxCalculations /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction Case 1 (the Form 8995 arm, which /qbiUsesForm8995A being false selects), and neither this fact nor /qbi8995aQbiComponent nor /qbi8995aDeduction carries an Export, so no line of the return transmits it. Widening the arm to the bare threshold test would be the tidier tree and is the right eventual shape, but it changes those resolved rows, so it is not taken here.

Fact.Name: Is complete
Fact.Description:
Whether this qualified business has been answered well enough to file. The single required answer is its qualified business income (Form 8995-A line 2 / Form 8995 line 1(c)): W-2 wages and UBIA are only read above the section 199A threshold, and requiring them would refuse every below-threshold filer, who never completes Form 8995-A Part II lines 4-12 at all ("If your taxable income is $197,300 or less ($394,600 if married filing jointly), skip lines 4 through 12 and enter the amount from line 3 on line 13", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8995a.pdf, page 1). The SSTB flag is complete-safe false, which is the conservative direction (no haircut claimed on an unstated SSTB is not a gap; a WRONGLY-claimed non-SSTB is caught by the filer, not by this graph).
WHAT IS REQUIRED DEPENDS ON WHICH FORM THE FILER IS ON, and that split is the correction to this fact's first shipped version. The QBI amount is always required. W-2 wages (line 4) and UBIA (line 7) are required ONLY when /claims8995A is true, because those are the lines a below-threshold filer is told to skip — but when Form 8995-A IS claimed they are not optional at all: the wage/UBIA limitation at line 11 is the entire point of the form, and an unanswered wages field drives line 5, line 10 and line 11 to $0 through the complete-safe views. The pre-migration graph refused that filer (its effective-amount facts read the raw writables with no fallthrough); the first version of this fact required only the QBI amount and so let the return FILE with a silently-zeroed deduction. Requiring lines 4 and 7 under the /claims8995A arm restores the refusal without touching any below-threshold filer. UBIA is required alongside wages rather than defaulted, for the same reason: $0 UBIA is a legitimate and common answer, but it must be ANSWERED, and the retired /qbiEffectiveUbia refused it too.
THAT JUSTIFICATION NARROWED and the requirement did not move with it, which is stated here rather than left for a reader to notice. "The wage/UBIA limitation at line 11 is the entire point of the form" is now true only ABOVE the threshold: the below-threshold line-13 regime at ../qbiComponent implements line 3's "skip lines 4 through 12", so a below-threshold filer on Form 8995-A does not read lines 4 or 7 at all. Keeping the requirement keyed to /claims8995A therefore refuses a below-threshold 8995-A claimer over fields nothing consumes. That is CONSERVATIVE (it refuses, it never over-deducts) and it refuses nobody the previous version admitted, so it is left alone here; re-keying it to /isAboveQbiThreshold — the condition under which lines 4 through 12 are actually worked — is a LOOSENING that owes its own witness.
UNIT B ADDS A THIRD, NARROWER REQUIREMENT and does not touch the two above: a business whose ../isPatron is TRUE must also answer both Schedule D (Form 8995-A) amounts, line 2 (QBI allocable to qualified payments) and line 4 (W-2 wages allocable to them). This clause is a STRENGTHENING and refuses nobody the earlier version admitted — an unanswered patron checkbox is complete-safe false, so a non-patron never reaches it. It is required because the complete-safe $0 on those two amounts runs the OPPOSITE way from every other default in this collection: an unanswered QBI amount UNDER-states the deduction (visible, taxpayer-adverse), while an unanswered allocable amount zeroes the line-14 patron REDUCTION and therefore OVER-states it. A silent over-deduction may not be filed, so the door catches it. The gate is ../isPatron, NOT /claims8995A: Form 8995's own header excludes patrons from that form outright ("you aren't a patron of an agricultural or horticultural cooperative", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8995.pdf, page 1), so a filer who says they are a patron owes Schedule D whichever form they think they are on.
THE QBI TERM IS RELAXED, THE ONLY LOOSENING THIS FACT HAS EVER TAKEN. All four arms now read ../hasQbiAnswer where they read IsComplete(../writableQualifiedBusinessIncome) before, which is that same test OR the per-business Schedule C derivation supplying the amount. The other requirements — wages, UBIA, and the two Schedule D amounts — are untouched, so no arm admits a return over any answer it refused before except the QBI one.
WHY IT IS NOT THE COMPUTE-WRONG THE effectiveQbi CONTRACT REFUSED. That contract's measurement (a) said a relaxation "when the fallback supplies it" ships a wholly unanswered business filing clean at $0, because the RETURN-level /qbiAutoDerivedAmount is Complete $0 on a return with no Schedule C at all — the floor supplies an amount unconditionally, so the condition is vacuous. The per-business fallback is conditioned instead on ../scheduleCLinkResolves, which is false unless the link is answered, the return claims Schedule C income, AND the linked Schedule C's own line 31 is Complete. A business with no link, a business linked to a Schedule C nobody answered, and a business on a return that never claimed Schedule C income are all still REFUSED here, each with its own witness. What files clean that did not before is a business whose Schedule C is answered — including one whose line 31 nets to $0, which is a fact about the business rather than about the interview.
THE RELAXATION IS PER-ITEM, which is what the N/N+1 pair pins: a second business that is neither answered nor linked re-refuses the whole return through /qbiHasIncompleteQualifiedBusinesses, however many of its siblings derive cleanly.
THIS IS THE SUBMISSION GATE, NOT A COMPLETENESS MECHANISM, and conflating the two is the failure mode the collection design warns about. The resolved graph under-claims for an unanswered business ($0 into line 16, visible and taxpayer-unfavourable); THIS fact is what stops such a return being FILED, through /qbiHasIncompleteQualifiedBusinesses below — the /socialSecurityReports/*/isComplete + /primaryFilerHasIncompleteSocialSecurityReports idiom, minus its hasSeenLastAvailableScreen term, which is a frontend flow concern this repo does not own (invariant #7).

Fact.Name: At least one qualified business is incomplete
Fact.Description:
Whether at least one entered qualified business fails /qualifiedBusinesses/*/isComplete — which asks for a different set of answers depending on the form and the filer, so this fact deliberately does not restate the list. Blocks submission — the socialSecurity:/primaryFilerHasIncompleteSocialSecurityReports idiom, which lives in its own module rather than in flow.
THE OTHER HALF OF THE COMPLETENESS SPLIT, AND UNIT B GAVE IT A SECOND JOB. Every per-item amount is complete-safe, so an unanswered business contributes $0 to Form 8995-A line 16 instead of making the whole sum Incomplete; that is deliberate, because completeness contagion would silently blank the deduction for the businesses that WERE answered. For the QBI amount and the wage/UBIA pair that $0 UNDER-claims: visible, taxpayer-unfavourable, refused at the door. For the two Schedule D allocable amounts unit B added, the same $0 OVER-claims — it zeroes the patron REDUCTION — so the door is not merely a courtesy there, it is the only thing standing between a patron who ticked the box and a silently over-stated deduction. Under- or over-claiming in the resolved graph, refusing at the door either way; this fact is the door.

Fact.Name: Two or more qualified businesses derive their QBI from THIS Schedule C
Fact.Description:
THE PER-ITEM HALF OF THE EXACT DUPLICATE TEST. True when more than one /qualifiedBusinesses item BOTH takes the per-business Schedule C derivation AND names THIS /scheduleCs item as the one it takes it from. A qbi-module fact living on scheduleC's collection, the same cross-module shape ../qbiAttributableHalfSeTax uses.
WHY IT LIVES ON THE TARGET COLLECTION, which is the whole of the construction and the reason the exact test was believed unreachable for four days. A duplicate test compares one /qualifiedBusinesses item's link against ANOTHER item's, and nothing in this engine binds an enclosing item inside a Filter or Find predicate — that much was true, confirmed by reading Filter.scala and Find.scala directly. What was missed is that the comparison never needed an enclosing ITEM: it needs a fixed VALUE every link can be compared against, and a member fact of the TARGET collection already has one. A Dependency on ".." inside a /scheduleCs/*/ fact materializes its own enclosing item as a CollectionItem VALUE (CollectionNode.extract answers PathItem.Member(id) with a constant CollectionItem node), and Equal compares CollectionItem values structurally by UUID (EqualOperator is x == y over a final case class CollectionItem(id: UUID)). The outer iteration is then carried by this fact's own per-item instantiation rather than by any operator.
THE IDIOM IS ALREADY SHIPPING, one type over. /filers/*/isTinUnique is Equal(Count(Equal(../tin, /filersWithTins/*/tin)), 1) — a per-item duplicate test written as a count of matches against the item's own key. This fact is that, with a CollectionItem key instead of a TIN, a GreaterThan 1 instead of an Equal 1, and the derivation gate below. Precedent for the ".." operand itself: /filers/*/isSecondaryFiler and /familyAndHousehold/*/isSelectedHohQP, both of which compare a designated item against "..".
THE GATE IS NOT OPTIONAL, AND ITS SECOND JOB IS COMPLETENESS. ../usesScheduleCDerivedQbi conjoined with the Equal restricts the count to businesses actually TAKING the derivation, which is what makes a shared Schedule C harmful rather than merely untidy. It is ALSO the term that keeps this fact resolvable: /qualifiedBusinesses/*/linkedScheduleC is deliberately un-Placeholdered, so on any return carrying a business with no Schedule C — a legitimate and common state — a bare Equal against it is Incomplete, and CountOperator returns Result.Incomplete outright on ANY Incomplete element (Count.scala's `case _ => Result.Incomplete`, reached because Result.unapply does not match Incomplete). Drop the conjunct and this fact goes Incomplete on that whole population, and the guard downstream resolves to nothing inside a SELECTED Switch case while carrying BlockSubmissionOnTrue — its own IsComplete wrapper tests the two COLLECTIONS and cannot save it.
THE GATE IS THE All's HEAD FOR LAZINESS, NOT FOR CORRECTNESS, and that is recorded because the adjudication which unblocked this fill asserted the opposite. AllOperator short-circuits on Complete(false) in BOTH positions — its apply matches the head and its accumulator matches every tail element — so a non-deriving business's Complete(false) gate returns Complete(false) whichever operand it is, and the gate-second variant measures GREEN across the whole fixture pack. Head position buys only that the Equal's thunk is never forced. The correctness requirement is that the gate is PRESENT.
TYPE: Boolean, complete-safe FALSE. Complete on every return: when /qualifiedBusinesses is answered every element of the All is either the gate's own Complete(false) or a Complete Equal (a deriving business necessarily has a Complete link, because ../scheduleCLinkResolves requires IsComplete(../linkedScheduleC)); when it is absent the IsComplete wrapper answers FALSE definitely, which is the true answer rather than a safe one — a return with no qualified businesses has nothing deriving from this Schedule C. Without that wrapper a bare Count over an absent collection resolves Placeholder, the same measurement /qbiHasIncompleteQualifiedBusinesses records.

Fact.Name: Two qualified businesses derive their QBI from the SAME Schedule C
Fact.Description:
THE EXACT DUPLICATE TEST. Blocks submission when ANY entered /scheduleCs item is named by two or more /qualifiedBusinesses items that take the same per-business Schedule C derivation — Count(/scheduleCs/*/qbiIsDuplicatedAttributionTarget) over zero. Each such business derives that one Schedule C's whole line 31, so the return counts one business's income twice.
THE PIGEONHOLE DISJUNCT IS RETIRED RATHER THAN KEPT, and the proof it is implied is short enough to state. ../usesScheduleCDerivedQbi is true only when ../scheduleCLinkResolves is, which requires the link to be answered AND the linked item's own line 31 to be Complete — so every DERIVING business points at a live /scheduleCs item. If the deriving businesses outnumber the entered Schedules C, two of them point at the same item, and that item's ../qbiIsDuplicatedAttributionTarget is true. The new body therefore refuses a superset of what the old one refused; keeping the disjunct would add a term that can never change the answer.
THE ESCAPE THIS CLOSES, which is the whole point of the rebody and is measured rather than argued. Two entered Schedules C and two businesses both naming the FIRST: counts are 2 and 2, the pigeonhole was FALSE, and the return FILED CLEAN with Form 8995 line 2 at 55,760.40 where 27,880.20 stands behind both columns and the second Schedule C's 20,000 reached no column at all. Direction of the escape: taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, the direction that files clean and therefore the one the scope mandate treats as worse.
WHAT THE DOUBLING COSTS, measured on the pigeonhole's own witness rather than argued. One Schedule C at 30,000, two businesses, both links answered, neither QBI amount answered: each business's ../scheduleCDerivedQbi is 27,880.00, /qbiSimplifiedAmount reports 55,760.00 against a /qbiAutoDerivedAmount of 27,880.00, and before this fact the return FILED CLEAN with a 6,426.00 deduction on a QBI figure worth 27,880.00 once. Direction: taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, which is the direction that files clean and therefore the one the scope mandate treats as worse. IRC 199A(b)(1)(A) allows "the sum of the amounts determined under paragraph (2) for each qualified trade or business carried on by the taxpayer" — ONE amount per business, which is exactly what a Schedule C counted in two Form 8995-A columns violates.
THE COUNT IS OVER THE DERIVATION, NOT OVER THE LINKS, which is what still makes an over-refusal impossible and is the one population boundary the rebody deliberately did NOT move. ../usesScheduleCDerivedQbi is false whenever the QBI amount is ANSWERED, so two businesses sharing one Schedule C while one of them types its own number contribute ONE deriving business to that item's flag and the return files. That return may still double-count by hand — a filer could enter one business twice and answer both columns — but that class predates the derivation, is VISIBLE (the filer typed the number twice), and is not what the derivation made silent. Widening onto it is a separate refusal with its own direction and its own witness, and this rebody does not smuggle it in.
THE OLD DENOMINATOR PARAGRAPH IS GONE WITH THE DISJUNCT. It argued that restricting the Schedule C count to items with a Complete line 31 would be vacuous; there is no Schedule C count any more, so the argument has nothing to attach to. The equivalent question under the exact test — whether an item whose own line 31 is Incomplete can be a duplicated target — answers itself: such an item cannot be the target of ANY deriving business, because ../scheduleCLinkResolves tests exactly that line 31.
TYPE/SIGN: Boolean, complete-safe FALSE, BlockSubmissionOnTrue — the /qbiHasIncompleteQualifiedBusinesses idiom in this same module, which puts a submission gate in the module that owns the data rather than in flow. The IsComplete wrapper is on BOTH collections and for the measured reason /qbiHasIncompleteQualifiedBusinesses records: a bare Count or CollectionSize over an ABSENT collection resolves Placeholder, not Complete, and a return with no businesses and no Schedules C has nothing duplicated in it and should say so definitely.

Fact.Name: This row claims an aggregation whose eligibility the return has not established
Fact.Description:
THE PER-ITEM HALF OF THE AGGREGATION ELIGIBILITY TEST. True when this Form 8995-A Part I line 1 row checks column (c) "Check if aggregation" AND any one of the election's three printed requirements is not established on the row: it is also an SSTB (requirement 2), its common-ownership attestation is not answered true (requirement 1), or its two-of-three factors attestation is not answered true (requirement 3).
WHY THE ELECTION NEEDED A TEST AT ALL, measured on the trunk this fill started from. ../isAggregation ships as an Export-only flag and NO fact in dictionary/ty2025/ read it, so a filer could check line 1(c) at no cost. The printed election is not free: "However, you may choose to aggregate multiple trades or businesses into a single trade or business for purposes of applying the limitations if you meet the following requirements" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 3, LEFT column), and the three requirements follow at lines 189-194, line 196 and lines 197-206 of the same LEFT column.
THE DIRECTION, which is why this is a refusal and not a disclosure, and which is MEASURED rather than argued. Aggregation exists to relax the per-column limitation: "You must combine the QBI, W-2 wages, and UBIA of qualified property for all aggregated trades or businesses, for purposes of applying the W-2 wage and UBIA of qualified property limitations" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 3). A business with QBI and no wages therefore borrows the ceiling of one with wages and no QBI. The two node tests that pin it carry the same economics entered both ways, above the upper threshold: as ONE aggregation row with QBI 100,000 and W-2 wages 60,000 the wage/UBIA limitation is min(20,000, 30,000) = 20,000 and the return deducts 20,000; as the two unaggregated columns it combines - QBI 100,000 with no wages, and no QBI with 60,000 of wages - each column's limitation is 0 and the return deducts NOTHING. The whole 20,000 is the election, and before this fact the graph granted it to any return that checked the box.
REQUIREMENT 2 IS EXPRESSIBLE WITH NO NEW INTAKE, and its numeric bite is small - stated plainly rather than oversold. Part I line 1 prints "Check if specified service" and "Check if aggregation" as columns (b) and (c) of the SAME row (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8995a.pdf, page 1), so a row with both checked contradicts requirement 2 on the face of the form. What it buys is the refusal of an internally inconsistent return rather than a corrected amount: above the upper threshold an SSTB row is already zeroed, and below the threshold no wage/UBIA limitation applies for the aggregation to relax.
WHY THE TEST IS PER-ITEM AND NOT A COUNT OVER THE COLLECTION. Requirement 2 forbids an SSTB INSIDE an aggregation, not an SSTB anywhere on the return. A return may hold an eligible aggregation row beside an ordinary unaggregated SSTB column, and refusing it would be a pure over-refusal - the failure a return-level Count(isAggregation) AND Count(isSstb) shape would produce, and the reason this fact binds the two flags to the SAME item.
TYPE: Boolean, complete-safe FALSE, and Complete on every return - which is a requirement rather than a convenience, because /qbiHasIneligibleAggregation Counts over it and CountOperator returns Result.Incomplete on ANY Incomplete element (the measurement /scheduleCs/*/qbiIsDuplicatedAttributionTarget records). All three operands of the Any are themselves complete-safe views of writables, so the Any is Complete whenever the item exists, answered or not; the gate ../isAggregation is complete-safe false, so a wholly unanswered row takes the False arm definitely.

Fact.Name: The return claims a Form 8995-A aggregation whose eligibility it has not established
Fact.Description:
Blocks submission when ANY /qualifiedBusinesses row fails ../hasIneligibleAggregation - the aggregation ELECTION claimed without the printed requirements the instructions condition it on. The mechanism, the direction and the measured 20,000-versus-nothing divergence are on that fact; this one is the door.
THE NAME SAYS "HAS NOT ESTABLISHED" RATHER THAN "DOES NOT QUALIFY", and the difference is the fill's one real decision. The two attestations are complete-safe FALSE, so this fact fires on an aggregating row whose eligibility is merely UNSTATED as well as on one whose filer answered no. The contract that grew this node left that default open and named the cost of each direction: defaulting to eligible preserves the silent over-deduction the node exists to close, defaulting to not-established refuses an aggregating filer until they answer two questions. The refusal is chosen because the error it prevents is invisible (the filer typed one combined column and the graph cannot see the components) while the error it causes is visible and fixable by the filer at the interview. The fact's NAME is written to match what the body does rather than the contract's phrasing, so no reader infers a finding of ineligibility from a return that merely did not answer.
WHY NOT THE COMPLETENESS DOOR INSTEAD. The unit-B precedent this module records - a patron whose unanswered Schedule D amounts over-state the deduction gained a third, narrower clause at /qualifiedBusinesses/*/isComplete rather than a wider default - was re-derived here and NOT copied, for a reason that outlives this fill: an ineligible aggregation is not an incomplete one. A filer may answer both attestations, answer them truthfully as NO, and have a perfectly complete return that still may not aggregate; routing that through /qbiHasIncompleteQualifiedBusinesses would tell them to finish answering questions they have already answered. The two doors refuse different things and both are wanted.
TYPE/SIGN: Boolean, complete-safe FALSE, BlockSubmissionOnTrue - the /qbiHasIncompleteQualifiedBusinesses idiom in this same module, which puts a submission gate in the module that owns the data rather than in flow. NOT a flow:/flowIsKnockedOut member, and that is a category judgment rather than a copied precedent: this is a user-input contradiction and data-completeness guard, not a scope limit, so there is nothing unmodelled for a knockout SCREEN to explain - the filer either un-checks line 1(c) or answers the two attestations. Its scope-sidecar revisit_trigger records that as permanent, which is the same ground that exempts /qbiHasDuplicateScheduleCAttribution from the dual-wiring lint. The IsComplete wrapper on the collection is mandatory for the measured reason both sibling guards record: a bare Count over an ABSENT collection resolves Placeholder, not Complete, and a return with no qualified businesses has nothing aggregated in it and should say so definitely.

Fact.Name: At least one qualified business is conducted with a specified cooperative
Fact.Description:
Whether any entered /qualifiedBusinesses item has ../isPatron true. The gate on the Form 8995-A line 38 section 199A(g) DPAD pass-through, and the mechanical form of the coupling unit B's contract insisted on: "Landing line 38 alone gives the patron the favourable half and none of the unfavourable half — an over-deduction."
WHY A DERIVED GATE RATHER THAN LETTING ANY FILER ENTER LINE 38, and it is read off the authorities rather than invented. IRC 199A(g)(2)(A) allows the patron deduction only "In the case of any eligible taxpayer who receives a qualified payment from a specified agricultural or horticultural cooperative" (26 U.S.C. 199A, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section199A&num=0&edition=2024), and the instructions say the same in operational terms: "You must complete Schedule D (Form 8995-A) if you're a patron in a specified agricultural or horticultural cooperative and are claiming a QBI deduction in relation to your trade or business conducted with the cooperative" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 6). The same checkbox that unlocks the favourable half therefore triggers the unfavourable one, per item, and a filer cannot take one without the other.
RESIDUAL, disclosed. A taxpayer with a section 199A(g) allocation but NO qualified trade or business entered here — the "If you don't have QBI, and only have REIT or PTP, skip Parts I through III and complete Part IV" filer of https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 6 — gets $0 at line 38 under this gate. That is UNDER-claiming, the safe direction, and it is also close to vacuous: a patron receives qualified payments from the cooperative in the course of a trade or business conducted with it, which is an item of this collection.
The IsComplete wrapper is the measured absent-versus-answered-empty distinction the rest of this collection's return-level consumers carry; see /qbi8995aQbiComponent.
A SECOND, DOCUMENTARY LEG: scheduleF:/form1099PatrsFromSpecifiedCooperative, true when a recorded Form 1099-PATR has box 13 checked. Box 13 is the PAYER'S own statement that "the information is from a specified agricultural or horticultural cooperative", which is the same question the per item ../isPatron checkbox asks the filer, asked of the document instead. Until this date a return could carry a box 13 Form 1099-PATR and still compute its QBI deduction on Form 8995, because nothing read the box; this leg is what switches such a return onto Form 8995-A, and that is real money in both directions (Schedule D's patron REDUCTION as well as the line 38 pass through, which is the coupling unit B's contract insisted on).
THE LEG SITS INSIDE THE IsComplete ARM ON PURPOSE, so the residual disclosed above is not widened: a return with no /qualifiedBusinesses collection at all still resolves FALSE, box 13 or not. The document can say the return HAS a patron business; it cannot say WHICH one, so the per item ../isPatron flag - the one the section 199A(b)(7) patron reduction runs off - is deliberately left as the filer's own answer. Wiring box 13 to a business needs a link from a payer document to a /qualifiedBusinesses item that does not exist.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 16 — total QBI component across all businesses
Fact.Description:
Form 8995-A line 16, "Total qualified business income component. Add all amounts reported on line 15". It is the CollectionSum of /qualifiedBusinesses/*/qbiComponent, and nothing else.
