The line 11 / line 12 GreaterOf that used to be this fact's whole body moved DOWN onto the item, where the printed form puts it — line 13 is a per-COLUMN line and always was, and line 16 is the only line that legitimately spans columns.
WHAT THIS FACT NO LONGER CONCEDES — BOTH HALVES, AS OF UNIT B. Its pre-migration Description said "With a single business and no patron reduction this equals total QBI component (line 16)". Unit A discharged the first half (the sum is real, over a real collection) and unit B the second: line 14 is /qualifiedBusinesses/*/patronReduction and the components this sums are genuine line-15 amounts, line 13 minus line 14. A second item is now SUMMED rather than refused, because Schedule C (Form 8995-A) loss netting — the reason the refusal outlived the patron reduction — is built at /qualifiedBusinesses/*/adjustedQbi. This fact's sum is therefore a real multi-column line 16 for the first time, and the retirement note where /qbiMultipleBusinessesUnsupported used to stand carries the test that was applied before deleting it.
THE /claims8995A GATE IS KEPT, AND THIS IS A DELIBERATE DEPARTURE FROM THE CONTRACT'S "BARE CollectionSum ... AND NOTHING ELSE", forced by a measurement the contract's own witness did not cover. The contract measured that an ANSWERED-EMPTY collection sums to "Complete BigDecimal 0.00" and concluded a bare sum was value-neutral. But this fact is INCOMPLETE — and therefore ABSENT from every materialized case — on every return that does not claim Form 8995-A today, because the whole line 2-13 ladder it read was gated on /claims8995A with no fallthrough. A bare CollectionSum would make it resolve Complete $0 corpus-wide, which (a) adds a row to all 938 committed cases and (b) propagates: /qbi8995aDeduction would begin resolving too, directly contradicting its own shipped Description, "Resolves only when Form 8995-A is claimed and its per-business detail is complete". Re-stating the gate here — once, at the return level, where the opt-in lives — reproduces today's resolution exactly. The contract's empty-collection measurement remains correct and remains load-bearing for /qbiSimplifiedAmount, which IS Complete $0 today and must stay so.
The IsComplete arm of the same When is the absent-versus-answered-empty distinction; see /qbiSimplifiedAmount's Description. It keeps an above-threshold claimer who has entered no businesses at all on the pre-migration refusal (Incomplete) rather than handing them a computed $0.
CONSUMER: /qbi8995aDeduction (Form 8995-A line 32/37), which reads this path as its line-27 term — unchanged. TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE (line 13 is a greater-of over two non-negative terms and line 14 is capped by Schedule D's own lesser-of), no rounding at this node.

Fact.Name: Section 199A(g) DPAD allocated from a cooperative (writable, Form 1099-PATR)
Fact.Description:
Form 8995-A line 38, "DPAD under section 199A(g) allocated from an agricultural or horticultural cooperative" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8995a.pdf, page 2), as the cooperative reported it to this patron. The form's own cap ("Don't enter more than line 33 minus line 37") is applied at /qbi8995aDpadPassThrough, not here — a Limit in this engine takes a constant and this bound is computed.
A REPORTED PASS-THROUGH, NOT A COMPUTATION AT THIS LEVEL, which is why it is a writable at all. The cooperative computes its own section 199A(g) deduction — 9 percent of the lesser of its qualified production activities income or its taxable income, capped at 50 percent of its W-2 wages (IRC 199A(g)(1), 26 U.S.C. 199A, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section199A&num=0&edition=2024) — and the patron's share is "identified by such cooperative in a written notice mailed to such taxpayer" (IRC 199A(g)(2)(A)(ii), lines 363-368). Nothing in this graph can derive it; the filer reads it off the notice.
THE REAL INTAKE IS FORM 1099-PATR AND IT IS STILL A GAP. The instructions say cooperatives "must provide the necessary information to their patrons on Form 1099-PATR or an attachment" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 1 and lines 4-6), and no Form 1099-PATR document exists anywhere in this dictionary. This writable is the same interim shape /writableQualifiedReitDividendsAndPtpIncome ships for Form 8995 line 6 — ONE manual entry standing in for a document intake; the document intake is not built. When that intake lands, this writable demotes to a taxpayer override rather than retiring.
IT LANDED: scheduleF:/form1099Patrs is the Form 1099-PATR document collection, its box 6 totals at scheduleF:/form1099PatrsSection199AgDeduction, and /qbi199AgDpad chooses between that total and this entry. Line 38 reads /qbi199AgDpad now. This writable is still the ONLY path for a patron whose share came on an attachment rather than in box 6, which the instructions expressly allow, so it is a live override rather than a leftover.
Min $0: line 38 is an addend to the deduction with no parenthesised entry field, so a negative entry could only be an attempt to reduce a deduction the form has no line for.

Fact.Name: Section 199A(g) DPAD allocated from a cooperative, from the payer documents or as attested
Fact.Description:
The section 199A(g) domestic production activities deduction a specified agricultural or horticultural cooperative passed through to this patron: the box 6 total across every recorded Form 1099-PATR (scheduleF:/form1099PatrsSection199AgDeduction) when any recorded document carries box 6, and otherwise the standing attestation /writableQbi199AgDpad, Incomplete and all. The idiom is the same as Form 8829 line 42: computed else attested. /qbi8995aDpadPassThrough reads THIS fact in its gate and in its LesserOf.
THIS DISCHARGES THE GAP /writableQbi199AgDpad NAMES. That fact's Description says "THE REAL INTAKE IS FORM 1099-PATR AND IT IS STILL A GAP ... no Form 1099-PATR document exists anywhere in this dictionary", and states the end state exactly: "When that intake lands, this writable demotes to a taxpayer override rather than retiring." The intake landed in scheduleF as /form1099Patrs, and this fact is that demotion. The writable is NOT retired and must not be: the instructions let a cooperative provide the figure "on Form 1099-PATR or an attachment", so a patron whose share came on an attachment still needs a place to type it.
THE GATE IS scheduleF:/form1099PatrsSection199AgDeductionAnswered, NOT the mere existence of a document, and the distinction is the whole safety of the edit: a patron who records their Forms 1099-PATR for the distribution boxes and leaves box 6 blank keeps their attested pass through, instead of having it replaced by a $0 collection sum. It is a real "was the source answered" predicate, not an IsComplete on a complete safe fact.
BYTE IDENTICAL ON THE COMMITTED CORPUS: no committed scenario carries a /form1099Patrs item, so this is the attestation term for term, and it passes the attestation's Incomplete through unchanged so the line 38 gate's completeness does not move either.

Fact.Name: The return has a section 199A(g) deduction passed through from a cooperative
Fact.Description: True when the section 199A(g) deduction allocated from a specified agricultural or horticultural cooperative (/qbi199AgDpad, Form 1099-PATR box 6 or the filer's entry) is known and more than zero. It is the fourth reason the Form 8995 header gives for claiming the qualified business income deduction. Complete-safe: false when the amount is unanswered.

Fact.Name: The cooperative deduction is claimed without a qualified trade or business
Fact.Description: True when the return has a section 199A(g) deduction passed through from a cooperative (/qbiHasCooperativeDpad) and no qualified trade or business (/hasQualifiedTradeOrBusiness false). Form 8995 has no line for that deduction, so this return works Form 8995-A, where line 38 carries it and lines 1 through 27 are $0 (or line 27 is the REIT and PTP component alone). Complete-safe.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 37 — QBI deduction before the section 199A(g) DPAD
Fact.Description:
The above-threshold QBI deduction BEFORE the DPAD: the smaller of the QBI deduction before the income limitation (line 32 = line 27 + line 31) or the income limitation of 20% of (taxable income before QBI minus net capital gain increased by qualified dividends) (line 36). Form 8995-A line 37. Resolves only when Form 8995-A is claimed and its per-business detail is complete.
RE-PATHED, BODY UNCHANGED. This was /qbi8995aDeduction, which stopped at line 37 and said so in its own authority comment; that path now carries line 39 (line 37 + line 38) and reads this fact. The split exists because line 38's printed cap is "line 33 minus line 37", so line 37 must be a fact the cap can read — writing the whole line-37 expression a second time inside the cap was the alternative and is worse. Every committed case is byte-identical through the pair: line 38 is $0 for a non-patron, and line 37 plus $0 is line 37.
THE REIT/PTP COMPONENT (lines 28-32) IS NOW MODELED and this fact is a REBODY: it used to take line 27 alone as the smaller-of's first argument, which understated the deduction for any above-threshold filer holding REIT dividends or PTP interests. Line 28 is the shared intake /qualifiedReitDividendsAndPtpIncome — the SAME path taxCalculations /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction Case 1 reads for Form 8995 lines 6-10, because the two forms' components are line-for-line identical (8995-A 28/29/30/31/32 = 8995 6/7/8/9/10) and the deduction must not jump at the threshold.
WHERE THE COMPONENT GOES, and the trap this arrangement avoids: line 32 is "Add lines 27 and 31" and line 37 is "the smaller of line 32 or line 36", so the component enters INSIDE the smaller-of's first argument. Adding it after the smaller-of would let it escape the 20%-of-taxable-income limitation, which is the one thing the printed line order forbids.
LINE 27 IS GUARDED, the above-threshold half of the outer-gate rebody. /claimsQbiDeduction is now Form 8995's printed DISJUNCTION rather than a business-only test, so this fact is reachable by an above-threshold filer whose only section 199A item is a Form 1099-DIV box 5 or a PTP Schedule K-1 — which is the point, because a gate widened below the threshold and not above it would make the deduction JUMP there. What that reachability requires is that line 27 be $0 for such a filer: Part I lists QUALIFIED trades, businesses or aggregations, so a filer who answered /hasQbiIncome=false has declared theirs not qualified and a filer who answered nothing and filed no Schedule C has declared none. The smaller-of's first addend is therefore Switch(/hasQualifiedTradeOrBusiness → /qbi8995aQbiComponent; else $0). /qbi8995aQbiComponent is untouched and simply not evaluated on the else branch; the SAME fact guards Form 8995 LINE 5 in taxCalculations /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction Case 1, so the business half is suppressed on both sides of the section 199A threshold or on neither. THE POPULATION THIS DOES NOT REACH is unchanged and disclosed at /claimsQbiDeduction: an above-threshold REIT/PTP-only filer who never answers /writableClaims8995A never gets here at all, because /qbiUsesForm8995A is false for them.
LINE 30's FLOOR IS THE COMPONENT'S OWN. "Combine lines 28 and 29. If less than zero, enter -0-": the GreaterOf against $0 sits around the whole combine, so neither a qualified PTP LOSS at line 28 nor a carryforward at line 29 can reduce the line-27 QBI component. LINE 29 IS REAL fill - /qualifiedReitPtpLossCarryforwardIn, an attested carry-IN stored as a POSITIVE magnitude and subtracted here, complete-safe $0 when unanswered. It used to be a hardcoded $0 with no writable at all, which was taxpayer-FAVOURABLE (a parenthesised entry field can only carry a loss, so omitting it could only OVER-state line 30 and with it lines 31, 32 and this deduction); an answered carryforward now moves that the other way. The SAME alias feeds Form 8995 line 7 through taxCalculations /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction Case 1, so the deduction cannot jump at the section 199A threshold. The carry-OUT that produces the amount is /qualifiedReitPtpLossCarryforwardToNextYear.
THE SHIPPING ARM IS PRESERVED VERBATIM as the else-branch, selected whenever the filer reported no REIT/PTP amount by EITHER route — which is every return in the corpus today, so the fill is byte-identical there and the old body stays under test. It would be arithmetically identical to run the new arm unconditionally (line 30 floors to $0, line 31 is $0, line 32 equals line 27); the explicit arm exists so the pre-fill behaviour has a live, named regression pin rather than an argument.
THE GATE IS WIDENED, AND HAD TO BE. It used to read IsComplete of the return-level writable alone, and /qualifiedReitPtpLossCarryforwardIn's Description disclosed in advance that this would become a real defect the moment a second route to line 28 landed: "WHEN /dividendReports/*/section199ADividends OR /qualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss LANDS ... the gate must be widened in the same unit or a filer with section 199A dividends and a carryforward will silently lose the carryforward." The first of those two landed with this change, so the condition became the disjunction Any(IsComplete(writable), box-5 total > $0). The strict > $0 spelling is deliberate: a box-5 total of exactly $0 contributes nothing to line 30, so routing it through the shipping arm is both correct and byte-identical, and the aggregate it tests is complete-safe so the guard can never resolve Incomplete. Line 37 carries no Round, so one dollar of box 5 makes arm selection observable to the cent here; on the Form 8995 side taxCalculations /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction rounds the whole Switch and a $1 boundary is invisible in the output — which is also why the widening is corpus-safe at the boundary.
THE GATE WIDENED A SECOND TIME, AND THIS TIME IT LEFT THE FACT. The other trigger /qualifiedReitPtpLossCarryforwardIn named — /qualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss — landed, so line 28 now has a THIRD route: a Schedule K-1 whose item D is checked reporting a box 20 code Z qualified PTP amount. Rather than add a third disjunct to this inline Any() and a matching one to taxCalculations /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction Case 1, the whole disjunction moved into ONE shared fact, /hasQualifiedReitOrPtpIntake, which both consumers now read. That is the structural half of the fix and it outlasts the routes themselves: while the gate was written twice, every new route to line 6 / line 28 had to be added in both places or the deduction would JUMP at the section 199A threshold, and one of the two copies lived in another module. The third disjunct is an EXISTENCE test rather than the box-5 disjunct's `> $0`, because qualified PTP income MAY BE NEGATIVE and a PTP loss must select the arm too.
AND ONE POPULATION THIS FORM'S SIDE NOW REFUSES: an SSTB publicly traded partnership above the section 199A threshold. Its amount would have to be reduced to the applicable percentage (phase-in) or excluded (above the upper threshold) through Schedule A (Form 8995-A) Part II, which this dictionary has only for /qualifiedBusinesses, so /knockoutSstbPtpAboveQbiThreshold blocks submission instead of taking the amount unreduced into line 28. THIS FORM'S SIDE DOES NOT REFUSE THAT POPULATION. Schedule A (Form 8995-A) Part II ships — line 16 /formK1s/*/sstbPtpQualifiedAmount, line 17 /sstbPtpQualifiedAmountBeforeApplicablePercentage, line 24 /sstbPtpQualifiedAmountAfterApplicablePercentage — and the rebodied /qualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss substitutes the reduced figure for the raw one before line 28 sees it, so an above-threshold SSTB PTP reaches this fact as a COMPUTED amount and /knockoutSstbPtpAboveQbiThreshold is RETIRED. The N/N+1 pair named above survives but is no longer a refusal pin: -boundary-at-threshold now asserts the unreduced $10,000 (Exception 1: at or below the threshold an SSTB is a fully qualified trade or business) and -one-dollar-over now asserts the COMPUTED $9,999.80, i.e. $10,000 x 49,999/50,000. The threshold clause itself still holds and the pair still witnesses it.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 38 — section 199A(g) DPAD allocated from a cooperative
Fact.Description:
Form 8995-A line 38, "DPAD under section 199A(g) allocated from an agricultural or horticultural cooperative. Don't enter more than line 33 minus line 37" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8995a.pdf, page 2). The reported amount (/qbi199AgDpad, which is the Form 1099-PATR box 6 total when the recorded documents carry that box and the /writableQbi199AgDpad attestation otherwise), cut back to the form's printed cap.
THE CAP IS PRINTED ON THE LINE, not an instruction-only refinement, and it is the statute's own limitation in the form's arithmetic: IRC 199A(g)(2)(B) says the patron deduction "shall not exceed the taxable income of the taxpayer determined without regard to the deduction allowed under this paragraph and after taking into account any deduction allowed to the taxpayer under subsection (a)" (26 U.S.C. 199A, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section199A&num=0&edition=2024) — which is exactly line 33 (taxable income before the QBI deduction) minus line 37 (the subsection (a) deduction). The GreaterOf against $0 around the cap keeps a pathological line 37 above line 33 from turning the cap negative and making line 38 reduce the deduction; the form prints no parenthesised field on line 38.
THE PATRON GATE, and it is the whole reason unit B could land line 38 at all. This fact is $0 unless /qbiHasPatronBusiness, i.e. unless some qualified business is flagged as conducted with a specified cooperative — the SAME flag that switches on the line-14 patron REDUCTION. A line-38-only unit is refused precisely because "landing line 38 alone gives the patron the favourable half and none of the unfavourable half — an over-deduction", and this gate is what makes that impossible to do by data entry as well as by design.
WHY NO FALLTHROUGH CASE. Both arms are gated on the same condition the line 2-13 ladder and /qbi8995aQbiComponent carry — /claims8995A plus an answered /qualifiedBusinesses — so this fact is INCOMPLETE on exactly the returns where line 37 is Incomplete, and /qbi8995aDeduction's Add stays Incomplete there rather than starting to resolve $0 corpus-wide. That trap is the one unit A recorded when a bare CollectionSum would have added a row to all 938 committed cases.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A total QBI deduction (line 39)
Fact.Description:
Form 8995-A line 39, "Total qualified business income deduction. Add lines 37 and 38" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8995a.pdf, page 2). The path is unchanged and so is its consumer — taxCalculations /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction Case 2 — but as of unit B it is line 39 rather than line 37: the line-37 body moved to /qbi8995aDeductionBeforeDpad and the DPAD it used to omit is /qbi8995aDpadPassThrough.
BYTE-IDENTICAL WHEREVER LINE 38 IS $0, which is every committed case: no fixture and no scenario flags a patron business or answers /writableQbi199AgDpad, so the Add is line 37 plus $0. And wherever line 37 is Incomplete — every return that does not opt into Form 8995-A — line 38 is Incomplete too, by the same gate, so this fact stays Incomplete exactly where it was.
THE DEDUCTION IS NO LONGER UNDER-STATED FOR A PATRON, which is what unit B bought, and the two halves move in opposite directions on purpose: line 14 (through /qualifiedBusinesses/*/patronReduction) lowers it, line 38 raises it, and a filer reaches both through the same Form 8995-A Part I line 1(e) checkbox.
THE BELOW-THRESHOLD PATRON NOW REACHES THIS FACT, and the paragraph this replaces said the opposite — accurately, then. Unit B disclosed that "taxCalculations /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction picks its Form 8995 arm on /isAboveQbiThreshold ALONE, so a below-threshold patron's Form 1040 line 13 comes from /qbiSimplifiedAmount and sees NEITHER the line-14 reduction nor the line-38 DPAD", and pointed at the split its own cap-boundary fixture asserted (this fact 9,250.00 against a deduction of 1,850.00). That routing was corrected in the unit contracted for it: taxCalculations /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction now selects on /qbiUsesForm8995A, which carries Form 8995's header conjunct "and you aren't a patron of an agricultural or horticultural cooperative" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8995.pdf, page 1), so the same fixture now asserts 9,250.00 on BOTH paths.
THE POPULATION STILL OUT OF REACH, narrower than before: a below-threshold patron who never answers /writableClaims8995A. /qbiUsesForm8995A keeps that opt-in as a CONJUNCT because this fact's own ladder is Incomplete without it — routing such a filer here would blank Form 1040 line 13 rather than improve it. That residual is not built.

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 10, QBI deduction before the income limitation
Fact.Description: Form 8995 line 10, "Qualified business income deduction before the income limitation. Add lines 5 and 9". This is the first term of the line-15 smaller-of, and it is the sum of the two components the form computes separately so that a REIT or PTP loss floored on line 8 cannot reduce the business component on line 5.

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 12, net capital gain increased by qualified dividends
Fact.Description: Form 8995 line 12, "Enter your net capital gain, if any, increased by any qualified dividends". taxCalculations:/qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction already subtracts exactly this pair from /taxableIncomeBeforeQbi inside the line 11 to 14 income limitation, as Subtract(taxableIncomeBeforeQbi, [income:/qualifiedDividends, scheduleD:/netCapitalGain]); adding the two subtrahends is the same quantity, named at the line that prints it. Both terms are complete-safe on a return with neither, so this resolves $0 rather than Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 13 before its zero floor, line 11 less line 12
Fact.Description: The subtraction Form 8995 line 13 makes before its floor: line 11, /taxableIncomeBeforeQbi, less line 12. Kept as a separate fact because the difference can be negative and the printed line 13 cannot.

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 13, taxable income before QBI less net capital gain
Fact.Description: Form 8995 line 13, "Subtract line 12 from line 11. If zero or less, enter -0-". The floored difference is the base of the section 199A(a) taxable income ceiling that line 14 takes 20 percent of. taxCalculations:/qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction ships the identical GreaterOf(Subtract(...), $0) inline.

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 14, income limitation (20% of line 13)
Fact.Description: Form 8995 line 14, "Income limitation. Multiply line 13 by 20% (0.20)". This is the section 199A(a) ceiling the statute states as 20 percent of taxable income reduced by net capital gain, and it is the second term of the line-15 smaller-of. The rate is the exact fraction 20/100 and the product is rounded to whole dollars at this line.

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 15, qualified business income deduction
Fact.Description: Form 8995 line 15, "Qualified business income deduction. Enter the smaller of line 10 or line 14. Also enter this amount on the applicable line of your return". The whole simplified computation lands here. taxCalculations:/qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction computes the same smaller-of for Form 1040 line 13a, rounding each printed 20 percent line, so the two are equal.

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 2, total qualified business income or (loss)
Fact.Description: Form 8995 line 2, "Total qualified business income or (loss). Combine lines 1i through 1v, column (c)". The graph already computes this sum inside /qbiSimplifiedAmount, which is line 4 before its floor and is written as Subtract(line 2, /qualifiedBusinessNetLossCarryforwardIn), the line-3 carry-IN stored as a positive magnitude. Adding that carry-IN back recovers line 2 exactly, with no approximation and with the Schedule C auto-derivation arm inherited for free: whichever arm of /qbiSimplifiedAmount's Switch fires, this fact is that arm's own value. Line 2 is also what lines 4 and 16 both say to combine with line 3, so naming it once keeps the printed column-(c) total and the two combinations reading the same number.

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 4, total qualified business income after its zero floor
Fact.Description: Form 8995 line 4, "Total qualified business income. Combine lines 2 and 3. If zero or less, enter -0-". /qbiSimplifiedAmount is that combination WITHOUT the floor, by its own name and Description; the printed entry carries the floor, and taxCalculations:/qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction applies it inline as GreaterOf(/qbiSimplifiedAmount, $0) before taking 20 percent. This fact is that floored value named once, so line 5 multiplies the number the form prints on line 4 rather than a negative combination the box can never show.

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 5, qualified business income component (20% of line 4)
Fact.Description: Form 8995 line 5, "Qualified business income component. Multiply line 4 by 20% (0.20)", rounded to whole dollars as the printed entry is. $0 when the return has no qualified trade or business (/hasQualifiedTradeOrBusiness false, for example a filer who answered that the business is not a qualified trade or business and whose deduction comes only from REIT dividends or PTP income), because line 1 then lists nothing; this is the same business guard Form 1040 line 13a applies, so printed line 15 equals line 13a.

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 8 before its zero floor, lines 6 and 7 combined
Fact.Description: The combination Form 8995 line 8 makes before its floor: line 6, /qualifiedReitDividendsAndPtpIncome, less line 7, /qualifiedReitPtpLossCarryforwardIn. The carry-IN is stored as a positive magnitude and SUBTRACTED because the line-7 entry field is printed inside parentheses, the convention its own fact already states. Kept as a separate fact because the value can be negative and the printed line 8 cannot, so the floor is a second step rather than a hidden one.

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 8, total qualified REIT dividends and PTP income
Fact.Description: Form 8995 line 8, "Total qualified REIT dividends and PTP income. Combine lines 6 and 7. If zero or less, enter -0-". The floor is what stops a qualified PTP loss, or a line-7 carryforward larger than line 6, from eating the qualified business income component on line 5. taxCalculations:/qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction ships the identical GreaterOf(Subtract(line 6, line 7), $0) inline; this fact is that expression named at the line it prints.

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 9, REIT and PTP component (20% of line 8)
Fact.Description: Form 8995 line 9, "REIT and PTP component. Multiply line 8 by 20% (0.20)". IRC 199A(b)(1)(B) makes the qualified REIT dividends and the qualified PTP income ONE component, which is why line 6 adds both halves and a single 20 percent is taken here rather than one for each. The rate is the exact fraction 20/100 and the product is rounded to whole dollars at this line.

Fact.Name: Form 8995 zero dollar floor
Fact.Description: The $0 constant that Form 8995 lines 4, 8 and 13 each floor against, every one of them printed as "If zero or less, enter -0-". The supported candidate templates have no unary positive part, so a floored line is written as a GreaterOf over this constant, exactly as form8959:/form8959ZeroDollarFloor and scheduleE:/scheduleEZeroDollarFloor already do in their own modules. Structural, not a statutory amount: it encodes the printed floor instruction, not a dollar figure Congress set.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 5 — 50% of this business's W-2 wages
Fact.Description: Form 8995-A Part II line 5, "Multiply line 4 by 50% (0.50)", a per-COLUMN line: half of ../effectiveW2Wages, which is the fact line 4 prints. PRINT-ONLY BY DESIGN, and nothing on the return reads it. The 50% leg is already computed inside ../wageUbiaLimit (line 10), which inlines lines 5, 6, 8 and 9 as one GreaterOf; this fact exists so the printed intermediate line has a fact of its own, and the two are the same arithmetic on the same input. ROUNDING, disclosed rather than absorbed: this fact Rounds its product while the leg inlined in ../wageUbiaLimit does not, so on an odd-cent wage amount the printed line 5 can differ from the line-10 computation by less than a cent's worth of rounding. Every printed line rounds to whole cents anyway, so the printed page is consistent; a reader comparing this fact to the line-10 internals should expect the half-cent, not read it as a defect.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 13 — this business's QBI deduction before the patron reduction
Fact.Description: Form 8995-A Part II line 13, a per-COLUMN line. DERIVED FROM LINE 15 AND LINE 14, NOT FROM LINE 11 AND LINE 12, and that is deliberate rather than backwards. The printed form states line 15 = line 13 minus line 14, so line 13 = line 15 plus line 14 exactly: ../qbiComponent plus ../patronReduction. LINE 13 HAS TWO REGIMES and ../qbiComponent already carries both of them in its own Minuend - below the section 199A threshold line 3's printed instruction skips lines 4 through 12 and enters line 3 here, and above it line 13 is the greater of line 11 or line 12. A forward GreaterOf over ../limitation and ../phasedInReduction would therefore be WRONG below the threshold (it produces the wage-limited amount the skip exists to avoid), and re-writing the regime Switch here would duplicate a body ../qbiComponent's own Description says is due a widening. Reading line 13 back out of line 15 cannot drift from what actually prints on line 15, in either regime, ever. NON-NEGATIVE and unfloored for the same reason ../qbiComponent is unfloored: both of its terms are non-negative on internally consistent answers, and the printed form floors neither.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 6 — 25% of this business's W-2 wages
Fact.Description: Form 8995-A Part II line 6, "Multiply line 4 by 25% (0.25)", a per-COLUMN line: a quarter of ../effectiveW2Wages, the fact line 4 prints. The first term of line 9. PRINT-ONLY, on the same footing as ../fiftyPctW2Wages above: the 25% leg is already inlined in ../wageUbiaLimit (line 10) and this fact gives the printed intermediate its own home. Same rounding disclosure: this fact Rounds, the inlined leg does not.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 9 — 25% of W-2 wages plus 2.5% of UBIA for this business
Fact.Description: Form 8995-A Part II line 9, "Add lines 6 and 8", a per-COLUMN line: ../twentyFivePctW2Wages plus ../twoAndAHalfPctUbia. This is the second of the two legs line 10 takes the greater of. PRINT-ONLY like its two terms: ../wageUbiaLimit already computes the same Add inline, and this fact is the printed line's own home rather than a new input to anything.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 8 — 2.5% of this business's UBIA of qualified property
Fact.Description: Form 8995-A Part II line 8, "Multiply line 7 by 2.5% (0.025)", a per-COLUMN line: 2.5% of ../effectiveUbia, the fact line 7 prints. Encoded as the exact fraction 1/40 rather than a decimal rate, which is what 2.5% is. The second term of line 9. PRINT-ONLY, on the same footing as the two wage rates above, and carrying the same rounding disclosure: this fact Rounds, the leg inlined in ../wageUbiaLimit does not.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 1 column (d) / Form 8995 line 1 column (b) — this trade, business, or aggregation's taxpayer identification number
Fact.Description: The identifying number the filer prints in the per-business table: Form 8995-A Part I line 1 column (d), and Form 8995 line 1 column (b). TYPED String, NOT EIN and NOT TIN, and that is the whole judgement here. The box is a UNION of three number kinds, in the instructions' own priority order: the employer identification number if the business has one, otherwise the owner's social security number or individual taxpayer identification number. The graph's EIN and TIN types each admit only one side of that union, and one printed box takes one fact, so a typed fact would refuse a legitimate answer for half the population (a sole proprietor with no EIN, or a partnership with no SSN). The precedent is /cdccCareProviders/*/pdfTinEinColumn, the String fact that prints Form 2441 line 1 column (c) "Identifying number (SSN or EIN)" over exactly the same union. THE COST, disclosed rather than absorbed: no format validation, so a malformed number is not caught here. A later unit that wants validation should build the cdcc shape in full (a writable EIN, a writable TIN, a Bool saying which the filer has, and a String selector over them) rather than retype this fact; the twenty-one sweep templates cannot express that selector, because a Switch returning an EIN has no expressible String default. AGGREGATIONS LEAVE IT BLANK by instruction, which an unanswered String models exactly.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 1 column (a) / Form 8995 line 1 column (a) — this trade, business, or aggregation's name
Fact.Description: The name the filer prints in column (a) of the per-business table: Form 8995-A Part I line 1 column (a) rows A, B and C, and Form 8995 line 1 column (a) rows i through v. The graph models the business itself (/qualifiedBusinesses) but has never held its NAME, so the printed column had no fact at all; this is that intake. Where the item is an aggregation the instructions direct the filer to enter the aggregation group name instead of a business name ("enter the aggregation group name, Aggregation 1, 2, 3, etc."), which is why the leaf is named for the trade, business, OR aggregation rather than for a business. Free text, unconstrained: the form places no format on it. NOT a Schedule C name pass-through, deliberately - ../linkedScheduleC is optional and a qualified trade or business may equally be a K-1 trade or a rental enterprise with no Schedule C at all, so deriving the name from the link would leave the commonest items nameless.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 27 - total QBI component carried into Part IV
Fact.Description: Form 8995-A Part IV line 27, "Total qualified business income component from all qualified trades, businesses, or aggregations. Enter the amount from line 16". THE GUARD IS THE WHOLE POINT, and it is not new law: /qbi8995aDeductionBeforeDpad - the shipped fact that prints line 37 - already reads line 27 as Switch(/hasQualifiedTradeOrBusiness -> /qbi8995aQbiComponent; else $0), the outer-gate guard, and this fact is that expression named at the line that prints it rather than a second copy of it written by hand. Since the outer-gate rebody, an above-threshold filer whose only section 199A item is a Form 1099-DIV box 5 dividend or a PTP Schedule K-1 reaches Part IV with no qualified trade or business at all; for that filer Part I lists nothing, line 27 is $0, and line 32 is the REIT/PTP component alone. Mapping the raw /qbi8995aQbiComponent here would instead leave line 27 and line 32 BLANK on a page whose line 37 prints a number, and the page would not foot. THE ONE DIVERGENCE FROM "ENTER THE AMOUNT FROM LINE 16", disclosed rather than absorbed: on a return that carries a real Part I/II detail line but answers /hasQbiIncome false, line 16 prints /qbi8995aQbiComponent while this line prints $0. On every return where the filer has not disowned their QBI the two lines are the same number. The else arm is /qbiZeroDollarFloor, the module's $0 constant, because a Switch arm must be a Dollar path.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 32 - QBI deduction before the income limitation
Fact.Description: Form 8995-A Part IV line 32, "Qualified business income deduction before the income limitation. Add lines 27 and 31": /qbi8995aLine27QbiComponent plus /form8995Line9ReitAndPtpComponent. This is the first argument of the line-37 smaller-of, which /qbi8995aDeductionBeforeDpad already builds INLINE; this fact is that Add named at the line that prints it. NOT /form8995Line10DeductionBeforeIncomeLimitation, and the difference is the one place the two section 199A forms genuinely part. Form 8995 line 10 adds its own line 5, the simplified 20%-of-line-4 component; Form 8995-A line 32 adds line 27, the sum of the per-business line-15 components from Part II. The REIT/PTP half IS shared - qbi.xml records that 8995-A 28/29/30/31 = 8995 6/7/8/9 line for line, which is why line 31's fact is reused unchanged - but the business half is not, so line 32 needs its own node. WHERE THE REIT/PTP COMPONENT GOES: INSIDE the smaller-of's first argument, never after it. Adding it after line 37 would let it escape the 20%-of-taxable-income limitation, which is the one thing the printed line order forbids. PRINT-ONLY until /qbi8995aDeductionBeforeDpad consumes it: that fact writes the identical Add inline today, so the two cannot disagree, but the duplication is real and the rewire obligation records it.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 22 - taxable income before the QBI deduction over the section 199A threshold
Fact.Description: Form 8995-A Part III line 22, "Subtract line 21 from line 20": /taxableIncomeBeforeQbi (line 20) less /qbiThresholdApplicable (line 21, $197,300 or $394,600 MFJ). RETURN-LEVEL, not per-column, because both of its terms are functions of taxable income and of filing status rather than of any one trade or business - the same reason ../phasedInReduction's own Description gives for keeping the phase-in percentage's numerator and denominator at the return level. It is the NUMERATOR of the phase-in percentage line 24 prints and line 25 applies, and /qualifiedBusinesses/*/phasedInReduction already builds this exact Subtract INLINE as the second factor of its subtrahend's dividend; this fact is that factor named at the line that prints it. Print-only: nothing on the return reads it. SIGN: positive only inside the phase-in range. Below the threshold the difference is negative, which is why Part III is skipped there and why this fact carries the render-gate obligation rather than a zero floor the printed line does not have.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 19 - this business's 20% of QBI in excess of its W-2 wage / UBIA limit
Fact.Description: Form 8995-A Part III line 19, "Subtract line 18 from line 17", a per-COLUMN line: line 17 is ../twentyPctQbi (20% of this business's QBI, the fact line 3 and line 17 both print) and line 18 is ../wageUbiaLimit (the greater of 50% of W-2 wages or 25% of W-2 wages plus 2.5% of UBIA, the fact line 10 and line 18 both print). The difference is the amount the phase-in ratably reduces, and it is the excess of the unlimited 20% component over the wage/UBIA cap. ALREADY COMPUTED, NEVER NAMED: ../phasedInReduction builds this exact Subtract INLINE as the first factor of its subtrahend's dividend, so this fact is that factor given the home of the line that prints it, on the same footing as ../fiftyPctW2Wages and ../twentyFivePctW2Wages, which name the legs already inlined in ../wageUbiaLimit. Nothing on the return reads it; it is print-only by design. SIGN: Part III is completed only when line 10 is less than line 3, so on every return that prints it the difference is positive. The printed line carries no floor and neither does this fact, so outside Part III's own conditions it can go negative - which is the render-gate debt the obligation records, not a floor this line is entitled to.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 25 - this business's total phase-in reduction
Fact.Description: Form 8995-A Part III line 25, "Total phase-in reduction. Multiply line 19 by line 24", a per-COLUMN line. DERIVED FROM LINE 17 AND LINE 26, NOT FROM LINE 19 AND LINE 24, and that is deliberate rather than backwards. The printed form states line 26 = line 17 minus line 25, so line 25 = line 17 minus line 26 exactly: ../twentyPctQbi less ../phasedInReduction, the shipped fact whose own Name already claims "Form 8995-A line 12/26" and which this form's line 12 and line 26 boxes both print. WHY NOT THE FORWARD MULTIPLY. Line 24 is a percentage this dictionary cannot yet name (no supported template renders a Rational quotient of two Dollar facts), and the nearest expressible forward form, dollar_prorata(total=line 19, part=line 22, whole=line 23), divides part by whole in Dollar space at two decimal places - it would round the phase-in percentage to a whole percent and could part from the line 26 the page prints beside it by several hundred dollars on a large column. Reading line 25 back out of lines 17 and 26 cannot drift from what actually prints on line 26, ever, and the three printed lines always foot. This is the idiom ../qbiDeductionBeforePatronReduction already uses on this form, where line 13 is read back out of line 15 and line 14 for the same reason. PRINT-ONLY: nothing on the return reads it; line 26 is where the value re-enters the computation, at line 12.

Fact.Name: Form 8995-A line 24 phase-in percentage times 1000
Fact.Description: Form 8995-A Part III line 24, "Phase-in percentage. Divide line 22 by line 23", carried as INTEGER THOUSANDTHS so the three decimal places the line needs survive: line 24 times 1000. The numerator is /qbi8995aTaxableIncomeOverThreshold (the printed line 22, taxable income before the QBI deduction less the section 199A threshold) and the denominator is /qbiPhaseInRangeWidth (the printed line 23, $50,000 or $100,000 married filing jointly). MULTIPLY FIRST, DIVIDE LAST: /qualifiedBusinesses/*/phasedInReduction builds this same quotient inline, and the reason /qbi8995aTotalPhaseInReduction reads line 25 back out of lines 17 and 26 rather than forward through line 24 is that a Dollar quotient taken at two places rounds this percentage to a whole percent. Scaling by 1000 before the divide keeps the third place. Capped at 1000 and complete safe 0 when the range is not positive; inside the phase-in range the numerator is between zero and the denominator, so the cap binds only at the top of the band. PRINT ONLY: nothing on the return reads this fact. The line 25 and line 26 the page prints beside it stay on their existing exact bodies, so the printed column cannot part from the computed deduction. ONE BOX, NOT TWO: the ledger records the row's other three fields as read only, so unlike Form 8863 line 6 this line has no decimal split and the single box renders through one three decimal transform.

Fact.Name: Schedule A (Form 8995-A) lines 10 and 23 applicable percentage, times 1000
Fact.Description:
Schedule A (Form 8995-A) line 10, "Applicable percentage. Subtract line 9 from 100%", and Part II line 23, which is the identical subtraction over the identical ratio. ONE FACT FOR BOTH LINES: Part I line 9 and Part II line 22 are both "taxable income before the QBI deduction over the threshold, divided by the phase-in range width", neither term is a function of any one trade or business, so the percentage is return level and the same number prints in both places. Carried as INTEGER THOUSANDTHS, the scale /qbi8995aPhaseInPercentageThousandths already uses, so the three decimal places the printed line needs survive; the box renders through a percent transform.
DERIVED BY SUBTRACTION FROM THE PRINTED RATIO, NOT BY A SECOND DIVISION, and that is the whole design judgement. The obvious forward build is a scaled ratio of (upper threshold less taxable income, floored at zero) over the phase-in range width, which is what /qualifiedBusinesses/*/effectiveQbi computes inline. It would be arithmetically right and typographically wrong: it rounds a second quotient independently, so the two numbers the page prints one above the other, line 9 and line 10, could sum to 1001 thousandths rather than 1000. Reading line 10 back out of line 9 cannot drift from what actually prints on line 9, ever. This is the idiom /qualifiedBusinesses/*/totalPhaseInReduction already uses on the parent form, where line 25 is read back out of lines 17 and 26 for the same reason, and its Description records the same argument.
SIGN AND RANGE. Inside the phase-in band the ratio is between 0 and 1000, so this is between 1000 and 0 and falls as taxable income rises. At and above the upper threshold the ratio's own cap binds at 1000 and this resolves to 0, which is the right answer: an SSTB above the band does not qualify at all. BELOW the threshold the ratio is negative and this exceeds 1000, which is NOT a printable answer, and no floor is added here because the form itself does not have one. Schedule A is filed only when taxable income is above the threshold, so the fix is the render gate the obligation on this fact names, exactly as /qbi8995aTaxableIncomeOverThreshold carries the same debt for Form 8995-A Part III.
PRINT ONLY: nothing on the return reads it. The reductions the percentage drives, /qualifiedBusinesses/*/effectiveQbi, ../effectiveW2Wages and ../effectiveUbia (printed lines 11, 12 and 13) and /sstbPtpQualifiedAmountAfterApplicablePercentage (printed line 24), keep their own exact multiply-then-divide bodies, so the printed percentage cannot part from the computed deduction.

Fact.Name: One hundred percent, carried as integer thousandths
Fact.Description: The constant 1000: one hundred percent expressed in the integer thousandths scale the section 199A phase-in ratios are carried in. STRUCTURAL, not a statutory dollar amount: it is the unit of /qbi8995aPhaseInPercentageThousandths, whose own Description explains why the ratio is scaled by 1000 before the divide (a Dollar quotient taken at two decimal places rounds the phase-in percentage to a whole percent). Its one consumer is /qbi8995aaApplicablePercentageThousandths, the 'subtract from 100%' line Schedule A (Form 8995-A) prints at line 10 and again at line 23.

Fact.Name: Schedule C (Form 8995-A) line 3 total of the trades, businesses, or aggregations losses
Fact.Description: Schedule C (Form 8995-A) line 3, "Total of the trades, businesses, or aggregations losses. Combine the negative amounts on lines 1, column (a), and 2 for all trades, businesses, or aggregations", as the POSITIVE MAGNITUDE the parenthesised entry field prints. The quantity is already computed: /qbiAggregateQualifiedBusinessLoss is /qbiTotalNetQbi less /qbiTotalPositiveQbi, and /qbiTotalNetQbi has the prior-year carry-in subtracted inside it, so that fact is exactly "the negative line 1 column (a) amounts combined with line 2", signed negative. This fact only turns it round. WHY A SECOND FACT AND NOT A MAPPING of the existing one: line 3 is printed inside parentheses, so the box carries the sign and the value in it is a magnitude. The register's own convention for a parenthesised box is a positive magnitude, which is why Form 8995 line 3 maps /qualifiedBusinessNetLossCarryforwardIn and line 16 maps /qualifiedBusinessNetLossCarryforwardToNextYear, both stored positive. Mapping the signed fact would print a minus sign inside the printed parentheses.

Fact.Name: Schedule C (Form 8995-A) line 5 losses netted with income of other trades, businesses, or aggregations
Fact.Description: Schedule C (Form 8995-A) line 5, "Enter in the parentheses on line 5 the smaller of the absolute value of line 3 or line 4", a positive magnitude printed inside parentheses. Line 3 is /qbi8995aScheduleCLine3TotalLosses (this batch), already an absolute value, and line 4 is /qbiTotalPositiveQbi, the shipping total of the positive line 1 column (a) amounts, so the smaller of the two is a plain LesserOf. It is the amount line 1 column (b) apportions: "Allocate this amount to each of the trades, businesses, or aggregations on line 1, column (b)". THE CAP IS THE POINT. When the losses exceed the income the schedule nets only as much loss as there is income to absorb and rolls the rest to line 6; /qualifiedBusinesses/*/lossNettingAdjustment apportions the UNCAPPED /qbiAggregateQualifiedBusinessLoss instead, which is why the printed column (b) reads this fact rather than that one and why a rewire obligation is declared on the column (b) fact.

Fact.Name: The trades or businesses aggregated into this aggregation
Fact.Description: THE NESTED PER MEMBER COLLECTION Form 8995-A Schedule B line 3 quantifies over. One Schedule B is one aggregated GROUP, which is one /qualifiedBusinesses row whose ../isAggregation is true, and the line 3 table lists the individual trades or businesses INSIDE that group, one printed row each, with columns (a) name, (b) taxpayer identification number, (c) qualified business income or loss, (d) W-2 wages and (e) unadjusted basis immediately after acquisition. The grain is a member of one aggregation, which no existing collection carries: /qualifiedBusinesses is one item per row of Form 8995-A Part I and an aggregation is ONE such row, so the members are strictly below it. The register declares the printed axis as "IRS8995AB /qualifiedBusinesses/*/aggregatedTrades rows 3", mirroring the nested "IRS4684 /casualtyEvents/*/properties columns 4" row. Line 4 totals columns (c), (d) and (e) and those totals are what Part II carries for the aggregation: when members are entered, the aggregation row's qualifiedBusinessIncome, w2Wages and ubia are the member totals. Schedule B prints ONE aggregated group per copy: "If you have more than one aggregated group, complete and attach as many Schedules B as needed" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8995ab.pdf, page 1). The register renders IRS8995AB once, so only /qualifiedBusinesses[0] prints today; the honest end state is an includeForEach over a Filter of the aggregation rows.

Fact.Description: Column (c) of the Form 8995-A Schedule B line 3 table: this member trade or business's own qualified business income or loss, before it is combined into the group. It may be negative, exactly as its Part I sibling /qualifiedBusinesses/*/writableQualifiedBusinessIncome may, and it carries no Min $0 limit for the same reason. Schedule B prints ONE aggregated group per copy: "If you have more than one aggregated group, complete and attach as many Schedules B as needed" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8995ab.pdf, page 1). Fact.Description: Column (d) of the Form 8995-A Schedule B line 3 table: this member trade or business's allocable share of W-2 wages, before it is combined into the group. PRINT ONLY until the aggregation row's combined amount consumes it, for the reason its column (c) sibling records. Fact.Name: Schedule D (Form 8995-A) line 5 - 50% of this business's W-2 wages allocable to the qualified payments
Fact.Description: Schedule D (Form 8995-A) line 5, "Multiply line 4 by 50% (0.50)", for THIS trade, business, or aggregation. Line 4 is the shipping /qualifiedBusinesses/*/w2WagesAllocableToQualifiedPayments. SIBLING, NOT DUPLICATE, of ../fiftyPctW2Wages: that fact halves ../effectiveW2Wages for Form 8995-A line 5, the W-2 wage limitation, while this one halves the wages allocable to the cooperative's qualified payments for the patron reduction. Different input, different printed line, different limit. It is the second arm of the LesserOf already inline in /qualifiedBusinesses/*/patronReduction, and it is print-only until that fact consumes it.

Fact.Name: Schedule C (Form 8995-A) line 1 column (b) - this business's loss-netting adjustment, sign reversed
Fact.Description: The shipping /qualifiedBusinesses/*/lossNettingAdjustment with its sign reversed, so that the amount Schedule C (Form 8995-A) line 1 column (b) prints inside its parentheses is a positive magnitude. A HELPER, not a printed line: the column itself is ../lossNettingReduction, which floors this at $0 so that a loss row prints nothing. The two facts are separate because the twenty-three sweep templates have no negate, so the reversal has to be a Subtract from /qbiZeroDollarFloor before a GreaterOf can floor it. NOTHING ELSE READS IT and it is deliberately unexported.

Fact.Name: Schedule C (Form 8995-A) line 1 column (b) reduction for loss netting, as printed
Fact.Description: Schedule C (Form 8995-A) line 1, column (b) for THIS trade, business, or aggregation, as the positive magnitude the parenthesised column prints: the sign-reversed ../lossNettingAdjustment, floored at $0. TWO THINGS THE FLOOR DOES. It makes a profitable row print its apportioned share of the loss as a magnitude, which is what the parentheses on the printed column mean, and it makes a LOSS row print nothing, which is what the instruction asks for: "Apportion the amount from line 5 among all your trades or businesses with QBI, but not loss, in proportion to their QBI". The shipping ../lossNettingAdjustment carries a third arm for a loss row, the add-back of that row's own line 1 column (a) that brings its column (c) out at $0; the printed schedule reaches the same column (c) through its own "If zero or less, enter -0-" floor instead, with column (b) left blank. IT READS THE MODULE'S OWN APPORTIONMENT rather than re-deriving one from line 5, so that the printed column (b) and the printed column (c) (../adjustedQbi) can never disagree, and so that the full-precision Multiply then Divide the module already performs is the number that prints. THE ONE DIVERGENCE FROM THE PRINTED SCHEDULE is therefore inherited, not introduced: ../lossNettingAdjustment apportions the UNCAPPED /qbiAggregateQualifiedBusinessLoss while line 1 column (b) apportions line 5, which is capped at line 4. The two agree on every return whose losses do not exceed its income, which is every return in the committed corpus; the obligation records the rest.

Fact.Name: Schedule D (Form 8995-A) line 3 - 9% of this business's QBI allocable to qualified payments
Fact.Description: Schedule D (Form 8995-A) line 3, "Multiply line 2 by 9% (0.09)", for THIS trade, business, or aggregation. Line 2 is the shipping /qualifiedBusinesses/*/qbiAllocableToQualifiedPayments, so this is a fixed-rate line and takes the Round(Multiply(Rational, base)) shape rather than a ratable allocation. Fact.Name: The return's QBI deduction is figured on Form 8995, the simplified form
Fact.Description:
THE RENDER GATE for Form 8995: the return claims a QBI deduction, its taxable income before the QBI deduction is not above the threshold, AND it is not on the Form 8995-A path. These are the same three conditions as the Form 8995 branch of Form 1040 line 13a, so Form 8995 prints exactly when line 13a is figured on it. A return above the threshold never prints Form 8995: the form's own header limits it to taxable income "at or below" the threshold. Form 8995 and Form 8995-A are alternatives, never both — "Use Form 8995 to figure your qualified business income deduction" is the simplified computation, and a filer above the threshold (or a patron) uses Form 8995-A instead. /qbiUsesForm8995A is already THE FORM-SELECTION GATE for that branch (/claims8995A AND the admission test), so stating Form 8995's gate as its complement is what keeps exactly one of the two printed.
Complete-safe: both legs are complete-safe Bools (/claimsQbiDeduction is the complete-safe outer gate on Form 1040 line 13a).

Fact.Name: Schedule A (Form 8995-A) is required
Fact.Description:
THE RENDER GATE for Schedule A (Form 8995-A), Specified Service Trades or Businesses. Three conjuncts, all of them the printed rule:
1. The return is on the Form 8995-A path at all (/qbiUsesForm8995A). EVERY 8995-A schedule attaches to Form 8995-A and to nothing else, so no schedule may render on a Form 8995 return. This conjunct is what keeps the four schedule gates below the form-selection gate rather than beside it. 2. Taxable income before the QBI deduction is inside the phase-in range (/isInQbiPhaseInRange) — the instructions' "Exception 2: If your 2025 taxable income before the QBI deduction is more than $394,600 but not more than $494,600 if married filing jointly, $197,300 and $247,300 for all other returns, an applicable percentage of your SSTB is treated as a qualified trade or business, you must complete Schedule A (Form 8995-A)". ABOVE the upper threshold an SSTB is not a qualified trade or business at all and there is nothing for Schedule A to apportion. 3. The return has an SSTB: a qualified business flagged as one (/qbiHasSstbBusiness, Schedule A Part I) or a Schedule K-1 qualified PTP amount from a PTP the filer declared an SSTB (scheduleE:/hasK1SstbQualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss, Schedule A Part II). "Schedule A (Form 8995-A), Part II, should be used for SSTBs that are PTPs, and Part I should be used for all other SSTBs."
Complete-safe: all three legs are complete-safe Bools.

Fact.Name: Schedule B (Form 8995-A) is required
Fact.Description:
THE RENDER GATE for Schedule B (Form 8995-A), Aggregation of Business Operations: the return is on the Form 8995-A path (/qbiUsesForm8995A) AND at least one /qualifiedBusinesses row is an aggregation (/qbiHasAggregation). The printed rule is "If you qualify and choose to aggregate multiple trades or businesses into a single trade or business, you must complete Schedule B before starting Part I" — an election recorded per row, which is exactly what ../isAggregation holds.
Complete-safe: both legs are complete-safe Bools.

Fact.Name: Schedule C (Form 8995-A) is required
Fact.Description:
THE RENDER GATE for Schedule C (Form 8995-A), Loss Netting and Carryforward: the return is on the Form 8995-A path (/qbiUsesForm8995A) AND either limb of the printed rule holds — "If any of your trades, businesses, or aggregations have a qualified business loss for the current year or you have a qualified business net loss carryforward from prior years, you must complete Schedule C (Form 8995-A) before starting Form 8995-A, Part I."
* CURRENT-YEAR LOSS: /qbiAggregateQualifiedBusinessLoss is strictly less than $0. That fact is "NEGATIVE OR ZERO by construction ... identically, the sum of the negative columns", so a strictly-negative reading is exactly "any row has a loss". * PRIOR-YEAR CARRYFORWARD: /qualifiedBusinessNetLossCarryforwardIn is strictly greater than $0. That fact is carried "as a POSITIVE MAGNITUDE", so the comparison is with the opposite sign from the current-year limb by design, not by accident.
Complete-safe: /qbiUsesForm8995A is a complete-safe Bool and both Dollar legs are complete-safe amounts.

Fact.Name: Schedule D (Form 8995-A) is required
Fact.Description:
THE RENDER GATE for Schedule D (Form 8995-A), Special Rules for Patrons of Agricultural or Horticultural Cooperatives: the return is on the Form 8995-A path (/qbiUsesForm8995A) AND it has a patron business (/qbiHasPatronBusiness). The printed rule is "You must complete Schedule D (Form 8995-A) if you're a patron in a specified agricultural or horticultural cooperative and are claiming a QBI deduction in relation to your trade or business conducted with the cooperative", and /qbiHasPatronBusiness is the fact this dictionary already built for that sentence — the gate on the line 38 section 199A(g) DPAD pass-through.
THE /qbiUsesForm8995A CONJUNCT IS NOT REDUNDANT. A patron is on the Form 8995-A path by the form-selection gate's own patron limb, but the gate is stated in full so the four schedule gates read alike and so a later change to the selection rule cannot leave Schedule D printing on a Form 8995 return.
Complete-safe: both legs are complete-safe Bools.
